    right="Item 11"

>
[Hunger Oil](/Equipment.aspx?ID=829)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Agents of Edgewatch</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=36" />
<trait label="Contact" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=37" />
<trait label="Divine" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=48" />
<trait label="Poison" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=126" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #160: Assault on Hunting Lodge Seven](/Sources.aspx?ID=49) pg. 66

**Price** 235 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 2 hands

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Single Action" /><row>Interact</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Rendered from the fat of corporeal undead creatures and infused with ghoulish magic, this yellowish oil causes its victims to experience stabbing hunger pangs that only living flesh can abate. If you eat at least a mouthful of humanoid flesh, you ignore the [enfeebled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=13) condition from _hunger oil_ for 1 minute. While under the effect of _hunger oil_, you regain only half as many Hit Points from [healing](/Traits.aspx?ID=89) effects unless you've eaten at least a mouthful of humanoid flesh in the last minute.

 **Saving Throw** DC 30 Fortitude; **Onset** 1 minute; **Maximum Duration** 6 minutes; **Stage 1** enfeebled 2 (1 minute); **Stage 2** enfeebled 3 (1 minute); **Stage 3** enfeebled 4 (1d4 minutes)

**Craft Requirements** Supply one casting of [_ghoulish cravings_](/Spells.aspx?ID=134).

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 17"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Hungering Maw](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2109)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=36" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Talisman" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=155" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 94

**Price** 2,200 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** affixed to armor

</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Free Action" /><row>([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561))</row></row>

 

**Trigger** You attempt a saving throw against a [possession](/Traits.aspx?ID=129) effect

**Requirement** You are a master in Will saves.
</row>

</column>

---

A shining onyx gemstone clutched in a pair of black steel jaws, this pendant is a potent defense against hostile spirits and other beings who commandeer the bodies of others. When you Activate it, you gain a +4 item bonus to your saving throw against the triggering effect. If your result prevents you from being possessed, the creature that attempted to possess you is subject to a DC 37 [_bind soul_](/Spells.aspx?ID=21) spell, which can trap it in the talisman as if it had recently died. The talisman's magic is exhausted after use, but a soul trapped this way remains imprisoned inside, as detailed in the spell description. Starting at the end of its next turn, the trapped creature gets a new save to end the effect at the end of each of its turns.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 12"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Hungry Lantern](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3940)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Battlecry!](/Sources.aspx?ID=268) pg. 145

**Price** 1,900 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This lantern is made of weathered tin and is cold and moist to the touch. The interior of the lantern, where a wick or candle would normally be placed, is filled with thick, black smoke, and there’s no way to open the lantern.

**Activate—Consuming Darkness** <actions string="Three Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [darkness](/Traits.aspx?ID=569), [death](/Traits.aspx?ID=571), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645), [spirit](/Traits.aspx?ID=737)) **Frequency** once per week;   **Effect** Pure, impenetrable darkness flows out of the lantern like smoke and simply eats the light. A 60-foot [emanation](/Rules.aspx?ID=2387) centered on the lantern is plunged into darkness for 1 minute. This darkness functions as a 4th-rank [_darkness_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1480) spell. When the darkness is created, it deals 6d8 spirit damage (DC 30 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2297) Fortitude save) to all creatures within the area. Any creature reduced to 0 Hit Points from this damage is destroyed entirely, leaving behind only a shadow that will slowly fade over the course of a year.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 11"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Hunter's Anthem](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2867)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=644" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [GM Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=218) pg. 242

**Price** 1,300 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** 2
</row>

<row gap="medium">
**Base Weapon** [Longbow](/Weapons.aspx?ID=436)
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This +_2 striking [longbow](/Weapons.aspx?ID=76)_ is carefully handcrafted from a length of flexible green-tinted wood, etched in a variety of runic symbols, and strung with a dawnsilver bowstring. When you shoot the bow in rapid succession, the echoing chords generated by the bowstring form a haunting dirge that evokes the inevitable end of all things. If you have the Hunt Prey class feature, the weapon gains the thundering rune on Strikes against your prey. 

**Activate—Song of the Bow** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You shoot an arrow thrumming with the song of the bow. Make a Strike with the bow that deals damage as normal. As long as the Strike isn't a critical failure, the arrow explodes in a 20-foot emanation around your target, dealing 5d10 sonic damage to creatures in the area, including the target, with a DC 28 basic Fortitude save. Any creature that critically fails is [deafened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=8) for 1 minute. If any creature in the area is [undetected](/Conditions.aspx?ID=39) or [unnoticed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=41) by you, you learn its location, making it [hidden](/Conditions.aspx?ID=22) to you instead. 

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 4"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Hunter's Arrowhead](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2343)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 153, [Pathfinder #145: Hellknight Hill](/Sources.aspx?ID=4) pg. 77

**Price** 80 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

A _hunter's arrowhead_ is meant to be worn as a charm, such as a pendant, or carried in a pocket or quiver. The arrowhead is etched with images sacred to the elven god [Ketephys](/Deities.aspx?ID=110). While you wear or carry the arrowhead, it infuses you with great skill at hunting, and you gain a +1 item bonus to [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=16) checks and attack rolls against any creature you've currently designated as your prey with [Hunt Prey](/Actions.aspx?ID=10). A _hunter's arrowhead_ is also a [religious symbol](/Equipment.aspx?ID=41) of Ketephys.

**Activate** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** You would miss with an attack made with a [bow](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=3);  **Effect** You gain a +2 circumstance bonus to your attack roll, possibly turning a miss into a hit.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 4"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[Hunter's Arrowhead](/Equipment.aspx?ID=483)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Age of Ashes</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Enchantment" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=61" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #145: Hellknight Hill](/Sources.aspx?ID=4) pg. 77, [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 153

**Price** 80 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn

</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Reaction" /><row>command</row></row>

**Frequency** once per day

**Trigger** You would miss with an attack made with a bow.

 
</row>

</column>

---

This arrowhead-shaped charm is not meant to be affixed to an arrow, but instead to be carried in a pocket or inside of a quiver. A _hunter’s arrowhead_ is etched with images sacred to the elven god Ketephys. If you carry one on your person, you are infused with great skill at hunting, and gain a +1 item bonus to Survival skill checks and attack rolls against any creature you’ve currently designated as your prey for the [Hunt Prey](/Actions.aspx?ID=10) ranger ability (note that the bonus to attack rolls is an item bonus, and therefore not cumulative with an item bonus from a magic weapon). A _hunter's arrowhead_ is also a religious symbol of Ketephys.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

>
[Hunter's Dawn](/Equipment.aspx?ID=674)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Extinction Curse</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Unique" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=161" />
<trait label="Arcane" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=11" />
<trait label="Artifact" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=253" />
<trait label="Enchantment" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=61" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #156: The Apocalypse Prophet](/Sources.aspx?ID=36) pg. 67

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** 1
</row>

<row gap="medium">
**Base Weapon** [Club](/Weapons.aspx?ID=2)
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

_Hunter's Dawn_ is a _+3 [greater striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=280) [speed](/Equipment.aspx?ID=304) [ghost touch](/Equipment.aspx?ID=297) [club](/Weapons.aspx?ID=2)_. However, the notched head of the weapon marks it as an atlatl, an ancient tool used for throwing [darts](/Weapons.aspx?ID=68) and [javelins](/Weapons.aspx?ID=71). You can use _Hunter's Dawn_ with a mundane dart or javelin like you would use a bow with an arrow; when you do so, the range of the dart or javelin is doubled, and the dart or javelin uses _Hunter's Dawn_ to determine its attack modifier and damage dice.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action to Three Actions" /> Interact;     **Effect** You swing _Hunter's Dawn_ and launch a magically conjured javelin at a target within 60 feet, making a ranged Strike. The javelin has the statistics of a javelin but gains the magical properties of _Hunter's Dawn_ and disappears immediately after hitting or missing its target. On a successful hit, you deal damage (3d6 piercing, due to the atlatl's _greater striking_ rune, plus your Strength modifier); in addition, a gazelle leaps from the hit target to one or more targets within 20 feet of the first, dealing 2d6 piercing damage plus your Strength modifier. The number of additional targets hit in this way is equal to the number of actions you spend to activate this ability (one additional target if you used one action, two additional targets for two actions, and so forth).

**Activate** <actions string="Reaction" /> ;   **Trigger** You hit a creature with a ranged Strike with _Hunter's Dawn_;  **Effect** The target is marked. Once per day, you can cast a 5th-level [_locate_](/Spells.aspx?ID=173) spell on the marked target, regardless of its distance from you or your ability to cast spells. This effect persists until it is dispelled (counterspell DC 46), the creature dies, or a new target is marked.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> Interact;  **Frequency** three times per day;   **Effect** You shave a curl of wood from _Hunter's Dawn_ and create a roaring fire within 15 feet. You can choose one of the following shapes for the fire to take: a 10-foot square, a 20-foot line, or a 15-foot cone. Each creature in the affected squares take 6d6 fire damage (DC 46 basic Reflex save).

**Destruction** _Hunter's Dawn_ can be destroyed only by placing it on the funeral pyre of a dead god.

</column>

This effect persists until it is dispelled (counterspell DC 46), the creature dies, or a new target is marked. Activate Single Action Interact; Frequency three times per day; Effect You shave a curl of wood from Hunter's Dawn and create a roaring fire within 15 feet. You can choose one of the following shapes for the fire to take: a 10-foot square, a 20-foot line, or a 15-foot cone. Each creature in the affected squares take 6d6 fire damage (DC 46 basic Reflex save). Destruction Hunter's Dawn can be destroyed only by placing it on the funeral pyre of a dead god.

---

This magical book has its official title, _The Grimoire of Lady Jayne Cutter_, written on an inside page in illuminated letters. Among occultists and other scholars, it's known by its colloquial name: the _Hunter's Hagbook_. The book is a grimoire created and used by a legendary Varisian monster hunter. The _Hunter's Hagbook_ can hold 100 spells but the following spells are always present in the book, can't be removed from it, and count against the total: [_blind eye_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1213), [_blood duplicate_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1214), [_caster's imposition_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1215), [_hag's fruit_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1216), [_ritual obstruction_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1217), [_web of influence_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1218)

 When you attempt a saving throw against a [coven](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=11) spell, you can immediately end the duration of a spell affecting you that you prepared from this book. If you do, the result of your saving throw is one degree of success better than your roll (for example, a critical failure becomes a failure).

</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Myth-Speaker</spoilers>

<traits>

<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #217: Death Sails a Wine-Dark Sea
](/Sources.aspx?ID=273) pg. 77

**Price** 225 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** 1
</row>

<row gap="medium">
**Base Weapon** [Club](/Weapons.aspx?ID=357)
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This spine and skull of a slain [hydra](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3064) has been picked clean by a carrion bird and crafted into this _[+1 striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2861) [ club](/Weapons.aspx?ID=357)_. In addition to its normal traits, the _hydra head club_ also has the [modular P](/Traits.aspx?ID=807) trait, as it can be manipulated to cause the jaws to spring open. Even in death, its head twitches independently. The creature’s famed regenerative powers are still present, despite the creature’s death; if damaged, the _hydra head club_ repairs itself at the rate of 1 Hit Point per minute, unless it has been completed destroyed.

**Activate—Reactive Snap** <actions string="Free Action" /> ([attack](/Traits.aspx?ID=540)) **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** You attempt a [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) as a Reaction;  **Effect** The _hydra head club_ snaps with a momentary burst of its former glory. Your Strike attempt deals an additional 1d6 damage. If your Strike misses, the activation does not count against the _hydra head club's_ activation frequency.

**Craft Requirements** You must supply a skull and spine of a hydra when crafting this weapon.

</column>

You sprout a second head, increasing your awareness, intuition, and cognitive ability but also causing your physical capabilities to be impaired as both minds struggle to control a single body.

**Benefit** For 10 minutes, you gain [all-around vision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=49) and a +3 item bonus to all Intelligence- and Wisdom-based skill checks. Once during the mutagen's effect, if you fail or critically fail a Will saving throw against a [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647) effect, you can treat the result as one degree of success better.

**Drawback** You are [clumsy](/Conditions.aspx?ID=61) 1 for 10 minutes.

---

This _[+1 striking ](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2861) [longspear](/Weapons.aspx?ID=361)_ of polished white bone features a tip of layered reptilian scales, compressed to form a sharp edge. Akki crafted this spear herself after she and her allies tangled with a [hydra](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=499) plaguing the marshes outside Aelyosos. She pressed the scales of the creature down into a spearpoint mostly through sheer stubbornness, granting it a unique ability.

**Activate—Hydra Swipe** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ;  **Frequency** once per hour;   **Effect** The spearhead unravels and elongates into a group of snake heads. Make up to three melee [Strikes](/Actions.aspx?ID=1167) with the _Hydra Spear_, each at a different creature within 20 feet. These attacks do not count toward your multiple attack penalty until all attacks have been resolved.

If not, its misfire check is DC 10. If you fail this misfire check, the organ bursts, dealing an amount of bludgeoning damage equal to double the number of weapon damage dice to you and rendering the _hydrocannon_ broken. **Activate—Tinker Shot** ([manipulation](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per minute; **Effect** You fiddle with the pressure regulator on the _hydrocannon_ and then make a ranged [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) with the gun. A successful attack has an additional effect depending on which modular configuration the _hydrocannon_ is currently in.
  • **Bludgeoning** The target is pushed 5 feet away from you; this [forced movement](/Rules.aspx?ID=2364) is increased to 10 feet on a critical hit.
  • **Piercing** The target takes a –10-foot circumstance penalty to its Speeds for 1 round.
  • **Slashing** The target takes 1d6 [persistent bleed damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=86).
**Craft Requirements** The initial raw materials must include the extradimensional organ cluster extracted from a [grodair](/Monsters.aspx?ID=694). Harvesting the organs of a grodair in this way differs greatly from the normal method; it takes an hour and a successful DC 22 [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35) check. On a critical failure, the organ cluster bursts and deals 4d6 bludgeoning damage to the harvester.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Unique" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=161" />
<trait label="Fire" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=72" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Poison" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=126" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 164

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** 1
</row>

<row gap="medium">
**Base Weapon** [Hand Cannon](/Weapons.aspx?ID=193)
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This _+2 [greater striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=280) [hand cannon](/Weapons.aspx?ID=193)_ is carved and crafted from a single large fang, worn with age and cracked with red lines. The tip of the fang has been filed down, but still leaks black fluid occasionally. It was fashioned from the tooth of the [tor linnorm](/Monsters.aspx?ID=287) Hyldarf by a half-Ulfen gunsmith from Tian Xia who sought the title of linnorm king. Though the smith failed to slay the linnorm, he did claim the mighty dragon's tooth and fashion it into a magic firearm that still drips warm venom. Hyldarf survived the encounter with her attacker and slew the gunsmith years later, though by then the smith had already bequeathed the weapon to his chosen heir and it was far out of her grasp. The linnorm still searches for her missing tooth, portending potential doom for the weapon's owner.

 The weapon deals an additional 2d6 fire damage on a successful Strike, plus 3d10 persistent fire damage on a critical hit. Fire damage dealt by this weapon (including [persistent fire damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29) and damage from Hyldarf's Venom) ignores the target's [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=72) resistance.

**Activate** <actions string="Three Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You call upon Hyldarf's power to gain the magic of a linnorm for a brief time. For 1 minute, you gain the effects of [_fly_](/Spells.aspx?ID=125), [_freedom of movement_](/Spells.aspx?ID=128), and [_true seeing_](/Spells.aspx?ID=344) as well as fire resistance 20.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per minute;   **Effect** You soak your shot in the fluid of the fang, imbuing it with Hyldarf's venom. The next Strike you make with Hydalf's Fang before the end of your next turn delivers the venom to the target.

 **Hyldarf's Venom** ([fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=72), [injury](/Traits.aspx?ID=97), [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=126)) **Saving Throw** DC 34; **Maximum Duration** 3 rounds; **Stage 1** 3d6 fire damage and [sickened 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=34); **Stage 2** 6d6 fire damage and sickened 2.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Gatewalkers</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Conjuration" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=33" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Structure" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=153" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #189: Dreamers of the Nameless Spires](/Sources.aspx?ID=195) pg. 76

**Price** 1,300 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk** L when not activated
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

While many of the magical wonders created by saumen kar have been destroyed, _ice forges_, while rare, still see use today among the few individuals who manage to discover and keep one of these portable treasures. When an _ice forge_ isn't activated, it appears to be a small anvil carved from a lump of ice no larger than an apple. While in this state, the _ice forge_ remains cold to the touch but doesn't melt in the presence of high temperatures. It can be used to chill a beverage in a small container, although those who venerate and respect these items' legacy would doubtless find this use to be insulting at best.

**Activate** <actions string="Three Actions" /> command, Interact;     **Effect** You toss the _ice forge_ onto the ground, and it immediately expands in size, transforming into a fully functional forge that appears to be made of solid ice. Expanded, the _ice forge_ is 10 feet square and 10 feet high. While the forge itself is cold to the touch, it won't melt in higher temperatures, nor will it cause harm to someone who remains in contact with the chill surface for an extended period of time. The forge can be used to work metal as a normal forge (although fuel must be provided)—the heat created by its use does no harm to the _ice forge_, nor does it transmit to the surface it sits upon, making an _ice forge_ an ideal solution for those who seek to use forges in areas where open flames or smoke would be dangerous.

 You can return an _ice forge_ to its handheld anvil form by spending a single action to issue a verbal command, which has the [auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=16) trait. Doing so immediately snuffs out any fire within the forge and leaves behind unused material or ashes. Once deactivated, the forge can't be activated again for 4 hours.

**Activate** <actions string="" /> 1 minute (envision, Interact);    **Requirements** The _ice forge_ is in forge form; **Effect** The ice forge casts [_creation_](/Spells.aspx?ID=54) (heightened to 5th level) to your specifications.

While many of the magical wonders created by saumen kar have been destroyed, _ice forges_, while rare, still see use today among the few individuals who manage to discover and keep one of these portable treasures. When an _ice forge_ isn’t activated, it appears to be a small anvil carved from a lump of ice no larger than an apple. While in this state, the _ice forge_ remains cold to the touch but doesn’t melt in the presence of high temperatures. It can be used to chill a beverage in a small container, although those who venerate and respect these items’ legacy would doubtless find this use to be insulting at best.

**Activate—Expand Forge** <actions string="Three Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645))    **Effect** You toss the _ice forge_ onto the ground, and it immediately expands in size, transforming into a fully functional forge that appears to be made of solid ice. Expanded, the _ice forge_ is 10 feet square and 10 feet high. While the forge itself is cold to the touch, it won’t melt in higher temperatures, nor will it cause harm to someone who remains in contact with the chill surface for an extended period of time. The forge can be used to work metal as a normal forge (although fuel must be provided)—the heat created by its use does no harm to the ice forge, nor does it transmit to the surface it sits upon, making an ice forge an ideal solution for those who seek to use forges in areas where open flames or smoke would be dangerous.

You can return an _ice forge_ to its handheld anvil form by spending a single action to issue a verbal command, which has the [auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=541) trait. Doing so immediately snuffs out any fire within the forge and leaves behind unused material or ashes. Once deactivated, the forge can’t be activated again for 4 hours.

**Activate—Ice Sculpture** <actions string="" /> 1 minute ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day;  **Requirements** The _ice forge_ is in forge form; **Effect** The ice forge casts [_creation_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1477) (heightened to 5th rank) to your specifications.

</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Usage** worn shoes

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

These ornately embroidered boots are crafted by Varki artisans to help their hunters and warriors as they cross back and forth over the snow and ice of their homelands. Empowered by the magic woven into them, these boots enable their wearer to ignore any uneven ground or [difficult terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=2366) caused by snow and ice. Additionally, while [Striding](/Actions.aspx?ID=2305) on ice, you can move 10 feet for every 5 feet of movement you spend, as icy blades grow from the boots. 

**Activate—Rough Ice** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You stomp your foot on the ground, creating a 10-foot [emanation](/Rules.aspx?ID=2387) of jagged ice on the ground that lasts for 1 minute before melting. This ice is [difficult terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=2366).

After you drink this mutagen, your skin continually renews itself, thickening into large, scaly patches.

**Benefit** For 1 minute, you gain fast healing 2 and automatically succeed at flat checks to recover from [persistent bleed damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29).

**Drawback** Your thickened skin makes quick movement difficult, and your excess skin flakes off with the slightest movement. You take a –2 penalty to Reflex saves for 1 minute. Any creature attempting to [Track](/Actions.aspx?ID=66) you in the next 24 hours gains a +4 circumstance bonus to their check.

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Abjuration" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=2" />

</row>

<row gap="medium">

---

Your flesh looks no different, but is cold to the touch. 

**Benefit** You gain cold resistance equal to your level and a +1 status bonus to saving throws against [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106) effects. 

**Payment** Liquids in your possession, including [potions](/Equipment.aspx?Category=15&Subcategory=18) and liquid [alchemical items](/Equipment.aspx?Category=6), freeze over the course of 1 minute and thaw 1 minute after they leave your possession. Frozen potions and elixirs take 1 minute to consume. 

**Hidden Condition** ([conjuration](/Traits.aspx?ID=33), [teleportation](/Traits.aspx?ID=156)) No more than once per week, the gelugon can move you like a piece on a game board to advance its schemes. The gelugon can appear and transport you and any items you're wearing and holding from your current space to a clear space within 500 feet (the gelugon need not see this location, but must know its relative location and distance from you). This effect doesn't transport any other creatures. The gelugon is unlikely to place you in a less dangerous space than the one you left. 

**Termination Clause** The contract provides you the benefits of “the eternal ice of Cocytus.” If you travel to Cocytus, [Hell's](/Planes.aspx?ID=18) seventh layer, and stand within an area at least 100 feet across that contains no ice and has a temperature above freezing, the contract is void. Such locations are exceptionally rare in Cocytus, and the efforts to create such an area are likely to attract unpleasant attention.

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Cheliax, Infernal Inheritence](/Sources.aspx?ID=372) pg. 80

<row gap="medium">

</row>

<row gap="medium">

---

Devils have learned much in their eternal lives, and you have access to some of their secrets. You gain the Additional Lore feat for Devil Lore, and during your daily preparations, you become trained in two Lore skills of your choice. Since these effects are temporary, you can't use them as prerequisites. Once per day, from any distance, the devil who holds your _bargained contract_ can invoke an evidence concealment clause as a single action with the [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561) trait, leaving you [stupefied](/Conditions.aspx?ID=94) 2 for 1 hour; you can't reduce the value of this condition by any means. 

**Activate—Delve Infernal Records** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You cite your contract's discovery of evidence clause. The contract casts _[hypercognition](/Spells.aspx?ID=1563)_.

The pages of this part-spellbook, part-bestiary are illustrated with all manner of creatures, magical and mundane. The illustrations shift and move around the page when examined.

[Illusionist's Hat](/Equipment.aspx?ID=5201)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Bastion of Blasphemies</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=683" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=637" />
<trait label="Occult" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=662" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #224: Bastion of Blasphemies](/Sources.aspx?ID=357) pg. 239

**Price** 500 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn headwear

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

The _illusionist’s hat_ appears as a tall, black hat with a wide brim and a colorful band around its base. Although popularly associated with themes of magic, this hat is more the province of the entertainer or even the charlatan than of a proper arcanist, and many wizards scoff at those who openly wear such items. You gain a +1 item bonus to [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) checks made to [Create a Diversion](/Actions.aspx?ID=2387) and to [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=50) checks made to [Palm an Object](/Actions.aspx?ID=2409). 

**Activate—What's In My Hat?** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** With a flourish, you remove your hat and sweep it before you. The _illusionist’s hat_ casts a 3rd-rank [_illusory creature_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1567) to your specifications, save that the creature created must be an animal. As long as you continue to hold your hat in one hand, you can Sustain this illusion as a free action. Unlike with most illusory creatures, you cannot use your actions to speak through the creature.

    right="Item 10"

>
[Illusory Backdrop](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3530)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Convocation</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=683" />
<trait label="Illusion" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=629" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=644" />
<trait label="Structure" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=704" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rival Academies](/Sources.aspx?ID=235) pg. 56

**Price** 900 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk** 3 when not activated
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This three-panel folding backdrop measures 5 feet tall and 3 feet wide and takes 2 hands to carry when folded up. It projects a preset illusion when fully unfolded. _Illusory backdrops_ are typically used by artists, bards, gallery owners, and the occasional politician, and common illusions include the tops of battlements with grand castles in the background, cozy bowers, and well-appointed rooms.

**Activate—Set the Scene** <actions string="" /> 1 minute ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645))    **Effect** You unfold the _illusory backdrop_, placing it on the edge of three contiguous 5-foot squares in a straight line. The illusion then emanates in a 15-foot cone from the center of the line, facing straight away from the panel. The illusion contains a scene that includes up to 5 discrete objects (usually foliage or pieces of furniture). The scene is static and lasts for 1 hour, though that duration restarts if the backdrop is refolded and then unfolded again. The appearance of the illusion is determined when the illusory backdrop is crafted and can’t be changed.

</column>

This pristine leather belt is made of treated and polished black leather with silver fittings; it features a pair of matching leather holsters that can each fit a one-handed firearm or hand crossbow.

>
[Immaculate Instrument](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3514)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=683" />
<trait label="Artifact" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=537" />
<trait label="Divine" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=579" />
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 203

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn or held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This object, made of silver light, takes the form of a small musical instrument, prop, or other tool associated with a specific art form. The holder of the _immaculate instrument_ never suffers from creative blocks of any kind and their work is always insightful and skilled. A character who uses the _immaculate instrument_ to [Perform](/Actions.aspx?ID=2401) or [Craft](/Actions.aspx?ID=2385) can attempt the check at mythic proficiency once per month, and as long as they possess their _immaculate instrument_, they treat any critical failures with these skills as failures.

**Destruction** If the holder uses the _immaculate instrument_ to intentionally produce a work that is not just mediocre or crass, but one that devalues the public opinion of the art form itself in a showing of at least 100 spectators, the instrument fades away in shame.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

</title>

</traits>

pfs="Standard"
>
Cursed Immaculate Instrument
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Cursed" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=567" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 203

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk** L

</row>

</column>

---

This _immaculate instrument_ has been cursed by the [sublime breath](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3408) it was taken from, causing it to warp, rust, or tarnish, though the holder of the instrument cannot perceive this and rationalizes away any attempt to explain the instrument's obviously cursed nature. Whenever the _cursed immaculate instrument_ is used to produce a work, the holder must succeed on a DC 16 flat check or the work fails, leaving the holder frustrated and raising the DC of subsequent flat checks by 1.

 When the DC reaches 20, the work fails as normal, but the holder continues to attempt it fruitlessly to the exclusion of all other activities, including eating, drinking, and sleep, until they expire or the curse is broken.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 10"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Immolation Clan Pistol](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1175)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Cursed" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=274" />
<trait label="Fire" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=72" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 160

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** 1
</row>

<row gap="medium">
**Base Weapon** [Clan Pistol](/Weapons.aspx?ID=197)
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This charred and blackened _+2 [striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=280) [clan pistol](/Weapons.aspx?ID=197)_ is coated in a thick layer of soot and grease and its retort sounds uncomfortably like a scream. Clearly at dangerous risk of misfire, this weapon claimed the life of its dwarven crafter shortly after completion and is haunted by that pained spirit. This ever-burning spirit keeps the firearm warm to the touch, regardless of surrounding environment.

 No matter how much you clean and maintain it, an _immolation clan pistol_ is always at risk of a misfire, and the flat check to avoid a misfire is DC 7 rather than DC 5. On a misfire, an _immolation clan pistol_ releases a blast of concentrated fire, dealing you 2d6 fire damage and 2d6 [persistent fire damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29).

 An _immolation clan pistol_ fuses with you when you first fire it. While you're fused with the _immolation clan pistol_, the pained spirit haunts your dreams, forcing you to relive its death each night. If you fired the _immolation clan pistol_ that day, you are unharmed by these dreams. If you didn't fire the _immolation clan pistol_ that day, but still possess it, you awaken fatigued. If you no longer possess the _immolation clan pistol_, the spirit of its dwarven smith is enraged by your neglect; you awaken fatigued and aflame, taking 2d6 persistent fire damage.

 Regardless, these nightmares possess clues to the spirit's life. If you take the _immolation clan pistol_ to the site of its creation and repair it with tools belonging to the tormented spirit, you might be able to break the curse. If the spirit is set free, this weapon becomes a _+2 greater striking [flaming](/Equipment.aspx?ID=295) [clan pistol](/Weapons.aspx?ID=193)_ with no other abilities or curses.

**Activate** <actions string="" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You allow yourself to become partially possessed by the immolated spirit bound to the clan pistol. For 1 minute, you look like a flaming corpse. During this time, you gain a +2 status bonus to [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7) checks and the immolation clan pistol becomes a _+2 striking flaming clan pistol_.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

fields.text: Item 10 Immolation Clan Pistol Rare Cursed Evocation Fire Magical Source Guns & Gears pg. 160 Usage held in 1 hand Bulk 1 Base Weapon Clan Pistol This charred and blackened +2 striking clan pistol is coated in a thick layer of soot and grease and its retort sounds uncomfortably like a scream. Clearly at dangerous risk of misfire, this weapon claimed the life of its dwarven crafter shortly after completion and is haunted by that pained spirit. This ever-burning spirit keeps the firearm warm to the touch, regardless of surrounding environment. No matter how much you clean and maintain it, an immolation clan pistol is always at risk of a misfire, and the flat check to avoid a misfire is DC 7 rather than DC 5. On a misfire, an immolation clan pistol releases a blast of concentrated fire, dealing you 2d6 fire damage and 2d6 persistent fire damage. An immolation clan pistol fuses with you when you first fire it. While you’re fused with the immolation clan pistol , the pained spirit haunts your dreams, forcing you to relive its death each night. If you fired the immolation clan pistol that day, you are unharmed by these dreams. If you didn’t fire the immolation clan pistol that day, but still possess it, you awaken fatigued. If you no longer possess the immolation clan pistol , the spirit of its dwarven smith is enraged by your neglect; you awaken fatigued and aflame, taking 2d6 persistent fire damage. Regardless, these nightmares possess clues to the spirit’s life. If you take the immolation clan pistol to the site of its creation and repair it with tools belonging to the tormented spirit, you might be able to break the curse. If the spirit is set free, this weapon becomes a +2 greater striking flaming clan pistol with no other abilities or curses. Activate Two Actions command, Interact; Frequency once per day; Effect You allow yourself to become partially possessed by the immolated spirit bound to the hand cannon. For 1 minute, you look like a flaming corpse. During this time, you gain a +2 status bonus to Intimidation checks and the immolation clan pistol becomes a +2 striking flaming clan pistol .

>
[Immortal Bastion](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1847)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 15

**Price** 70,000 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn armor

**Bulk** 5
</row>

<row gap="medium">
**Base Armor** [Bastion Plate](/Armor.aspx?ID=17)
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This impressive _+3 [greater resilient](/Equipment.aspx?ID=279) [greater fortification](/Equipment.aspx?ID=285) [bastion plate](/Armor.aspx?ID=17)_ is built like an impregnable castle, with multiple layers of defense and no weak points. When you activate the armor's deflect melee trait, you gain a +2 circumstance bonus to AC against melee attacks instead of +1, and you gain 10 temporary Hit Points that last until the start of your next turn.

**Activate** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** You are reduced to 0 Hit Points or would die from a [death](/Traits.aspx?ID=40) effect;  **Effect** You drop to 1 Hit Point instead of being reduced to 0 HP or dying, and you gain 100 temporary Hit Points that last until the start of your next turn.

**Activate** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** You would gain or increase the [doomed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=9) or [wounded](/Conditions.aspx?ID=42) condition;  **Effect** You avoid gaining or increasing the condition. If the triggering effect imposes both doomed and wounded, choose only one to prevent. This doesn't remove either of the conditions if you already have them, nor does it prevent the same triggering effect from giving or increasing the prevented condition later.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 12

**Price** 1,800 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** etched onto armor

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This rune utilizes magical principles to manipulate gravity and turn you into an immovable object.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** Your armor anchors you in place, even defying gravity, rendering you [immobilized](/Conditions.aspx?ID=24) until you Dismiss the Activation. while you're immobilized in this way, you can be moved only if a creature succeeds at a DC 40 [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) check to [Force Open](/Actions.aspx?ID=34) your armor. You can also be moved if 8,000 pounds of pressure are placed upon you, though this is likely fatal.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 9"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Immovable Arm](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1368)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Transmutation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=157" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Grand Bazaar](/Sources.aspx?ID=100) pg. 73

_[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) All Pathfinder Society agents also have access to all assistive items from Morhen’s Mobility Apparel_

**Price** 700 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn

**Bulk** 1
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

The flat iron bar of an [_immovable rod_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=259) has been worked into the core frame of this prosthetic arm, a small button discreetly placed at the heel of the hand.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> Interact;     **Effect** You curl your fingers inward to press the button on the heel of your hand, anchoring your prosthetic arm in place. Your arm no longer moves, defying gravity if necessary. You can still move the fingers of this hand and your elbow, shoulder, and rest of your body while the magic is in effect, but you can't move your wrist. If you press the button again, the rod inside your arm is deactivated, ending the magic that anchors it in place. While anchored, the arm can be moved only if 8,000 pounds of pressure is placed upon it or if a creature succeeds at a DC 40 [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) check to [Force Open](/Actions.aspx?ID=34) your arm. A creature can notice the button hidden in the hand of the prosthesis with a successful DC 25 Perception check to [Seek](/Actions.aspx?ID=84).

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

Activate Single Action Interact; Effect You push the button to anchor the rod in place. It doesn’t move, defying gravity if need be. >
[Immovable Tripod](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1218)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 182

_[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) Characters with access to firearms gain access to accessories that can be used with those weapons._

**Price** 700 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk** 1
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This copper [tripod](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1207) has a magical core that can't be moved once magically locked in place—a perfect example of engineering ingenuity applied to magic items. This eccentric magical power is put to a pragmatic use of stabilizing weapons without the need for solid ground on which to stabilize them. In addition to extraplanar and aquatic environments, these devices have seen use by flying and climbing snipers who would otherwise have no way to mitigate their weapons' fierce kickback. 

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645))    **Effect** You deploy the tripod and press a button to lock it into place, allowing you to deploy the tripod in midair, underwater, or anywhere else where you don't have a solid horizontal surface available. If you Activate the tripod by pushing the button again, you release and retrieve the tripod. While anchored, the tripod can be moved only if 8,000 pounds of pressure are applied to it or if a creature uses Athletics to [Force Open](/Actions.aspx?ID=2375) the tripod with a DC of 40 (though most intelligent creatures can just push the button to release the tripod).

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

>
[Imp Shot](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2052)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=36" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 82

**Price** 24 gp

<row gap="medium">
**Ammunition** any

</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Single Action" /><row>([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561))</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This black-and-red ammunition contains an egg-shaped capsule. When an activated _imp shot_ hits, the capsule cracks open and releases a manifestation that resembles a Tiny [imp](/Monsters.aspx?ID=109) that can't act in any way or provide benefits outside those described here. If the Strike misses the target, the imp appears, makes a rude gesture at you, and vanishes in a puff of sulfuric smoke. On a hit, though, the imp harries the target for up to 1 minute, remaining in the target's space, slapping, nipping, hurling insults, and moving with the target as it moves. A creature harried by the imp is [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) and takes a –2 circumstance penalty to attack rolls and skill checks. At the start of your turn on each round while the imp is active, you must attempt a DC 11 flat check. On a failure, the imp makes a final vulgar gesture at the target and vanishes in a cloud of brimstone.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 70

_[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) All Pathfinder Society agents have access to all uncommon clockwork items and gadgets from Chapters 1 and 2 of this book_

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn over armor and clothes

**Bulk** L
</row>

**Access**  Due to the use of technology, all gadgets are uncommon or rare, though inventors and regions with access to inventors have access to uncommon gadgets.

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><row>see below</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

While you're wearing an impact foam chassis wrapped around your body, it Activates automatically whenever you fall at least 10 feet, causing a layer of soft, flexible impact foam to expand beneath and around you to cushion the fall. The impact foam decreases the falling damage by up to the listed amount, taking damage equal to the amount of falling damage the foam reduced. If this is enough to destroy the foam, it disperses immediately. However, if the foam has any Hit Points remaining, it remains surrounding you for up to 1 minute. While you're surrounded in foam, you are [immobilized](/Conditions.aspx?ID=24) and have standard cover against other creatures, and other creatures have standard cover against you. The foam has an [Escape](/Actions.aspx?ID=79) DC of 15; a creature can also remove it by spending three Interact actions. You or others can also attack the foam (the foam has an AC of 12), which disperses if reduced to 0 Hit Points.

<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><row>see below</row></row>

---

While you're wearing an impact foam chassis wrapped around your body, it Activates automatically whenever you fall at least 10 feet, causing a layer of soft, flexible impact foam to expand beneath and around you to cushion the fall. The impact foam decreases the falling damage by up to the listed amount, taking damage equal to the amount of falling damage the foam reduced. If this is enough to destroy the foam, it disperses immediately. However, if the foam has any Hit Points remaining, it remains surrounding you for up to 1 minute. While you're surrounded in foam, you are [immobilized](/Conditions.aspx?ID=24) and have standard cover against other creatures, and other creatures have standard cover against you. The foam has an [Escape](/Actions.aspx?ID=79) DC of 15; a creature can also remove it by spending three Interact actions. You or others can also attack the foam (the foam has an AC of 12), which disperses if reduced to 0 Hit Points.

    level="1"
    right="Item 17"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Impenetrable Scale](/Equipment.aspx?ID=154)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Abjuration" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=2" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Core Rulebook](/Sources.aspx?ID=1) pg. 558

**Price** 12,800 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn armor

**Bulk** 3
</row>

<row gap="medium">
**Base Armor** [Scale Mail](/Armor.aspx?ID=8)
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Made of overlapping, lustrous black scales of standard-grade adamantine, this _+2 greater resilient [fortification](/Equipment.aspx?ID=285) [adamantine](/Equipment.aspx?ID=139) [scale mail](/Armor.aspx?ID=8)_ seems to momentarily thicken at the point of impact when hit. Whenever the armor’s _fortification_ rune successfully turns a significant foe’s critical hit into a normal hit, one of the scales on the armor turns violet. You gain resistance to physical damage equal to the number of violet scales, to a maximum of 8.

 At dawn each day, all the violet scales return to normal.

**Craft Requirements** The initial raw materials must include 1,600 gp of adamantine.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Transmutation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=157" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Grand Bazaar](/Sources.aspx?ID=100) pg. 80

_[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) The effects of the implacable rune only activate when an enemy causes the effect to apply._

**Price** 1,200 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** etched onto medium or heavy armor

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This substantial rune makes you difficult to hold back. Whenever you are affected by an effect that lasts until you [Escape](/Actions.aspx?ID=79) (for instance, from the [Grapple](/Actions.aspx?ID=35) action or a [tanglefoot bag](/Equipment.aspx?ID=78)), you become [quickened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=32). You can use the extra action each round only to Step or Escape.

fields.text: Item 11 Implacable Uncommon Magical Transmutation Source Grand Bazaar pg. 80 PFS Note The effects of the implacable rune only activate when an enemy causes the effect to apply. Price 1,200 gp Usage etched onto medium or heavy armor This substantial rune makes you difficult to hold back. Whenever you are affected by an effect that lasts until you Escape (for instance, from the Grapple action or a tanglefoot bag), you become quickened. You can use the extra action each round only to Step or Escape.

It's effective at weakening [water elementals](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=45), [air elementals](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=41), [ooze](/Traits.aspx?ID=122), and other creatures the GM determines are similarly amorphous, which can even include particularly gelatinous [aberrations](/Traits.aspx?ID=1). You release the dust toward one creature within 5 feet of you, which must attempt a Fortitude saving throw. The target must repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns. Implosion dust functions for up to 6 rounds. It then becomes inert, and the creature returns to its normal size. **Critical Success** The dust becomes inert, and the creature returns to its normal size.
**Success** The target increases in size one step, up to its normal size. If it's at its normal size after the increase, the effect ends.
**Failure** The target decreases in size one step, to a minimum of Tiny. </title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Hellbreakers</spoilers>

<traits>

<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=644" />

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #222: Hellbreakers](/Sources.aspx?ID=307) pg. 213

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk** 1
</row>

<row gap="medium">
**Base Shield** [Steel Shield](/Shields.aspx?ID=19)
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

A favorite of Hellknights, this [steel shield](/Shields.aspx?ID=19) (Hardness 6, HP 36, BT 18) is often emblazoned with the symbol of a Hellknight order and often notched with the number of times it has absorbed damage.

**Activate—Terrifying Block** <actions string="Free Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=590), [fear](/Traits.aspx?ID=598), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647)) **Frequency** once per 10 minutes; **Trigger** You [Shield Block](/Feats.aspx?ID=5212);  **Effect** When a weapon strikes an _imposing shield_, the sigil glows with a chilling light. The creature that made the attack that triggered your Shield Block becomes [frightened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=76) 2. If the Shield Block reduced the incoming damage to 0, the creature instead becomes frightened 3.

</column>

</title>

<traits>

</traits>

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 33

**Price** 70,000 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** etched onto a weapon

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This rune makes a weapon capable of impossible offense and defense. The etched weapon is immune to [_dispel magic_](/Spells.aspx?ID=78) and similar effects that could [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) its magic. If it's a ranged weapon or [thrown](/Traits.aspx?ID=195) weapon, its range increment is doubled.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [teleportation](/Traits.aspx?ID=710)) **Frequency** once per hour;   **Effect** You and the weapon flash to a perfect attacking position, then return to where you started. Make a Strike with the etched weapon against one creature you can see, even if the target is beyond the weapon's reach or range. On this Strike, ignore any circumstance penalty, status penalty, and range increment penalty.

</column>

This sleight-of-hand for the taste buds is flavored with absinthe and honey and always resembles something completely unlike a cake, from a pile of armor to a bowl of soup. Eating the cake gives you the confidence to make the impossible seem possible: for 10 minutes after the meal, you gain a +2 item bonus to your [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) checks to [Impersonate](/Actions.aspx?ID=46), as well as to [Lie](/Actions.aspx?ID=47) to convince others that you possess knowledge about the type of item that the cake resembles.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 8"
    pfs=""
>
[In the Shadows of Toil](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1731)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Crown of the Kobold King</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Unique" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=161" />
<trait label="Grimoire" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=387" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Necromancy" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=117" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Crown of the Kobold King](/Sources.aspx?ID=148) pg. 116

**Price** 500 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

_In the Shadows of Toil_ was originally an incomplete copy of a journal kept by the dwarven adventurer Druingar the Glintaxe. Drazmorg made extensive use of the book's wide margins and several dozen blank pages left in the back to serve as a spellbook. Over the years, he further enhanced his copy to transform it into a grimoire (see [here](/Rules.aspx?ID=1494) full rules on grimoires). A character who reads [Necril](/Languages.aspx?ID=20) can learn about Drazmorg's history, his discovery of the Third Seal, and his hopes to absorb all of its power before seeking out the [Whispering Way](/Deities.aspx?ID=24) to lead them on a new crusade to hunt down the next two seals, destroy them, and bring back the Whispering Tyrant. Beyond these frightening notes, the grimoire also contains copies of all the spells Drazmorg has prepared and those needed to recharge [his staff](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1728); feel free to add more spells to this list if you wish.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> envision ([metamagic](/Traits.aspx?ID=107)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** If your next action is to cast a [necromancy](/Traits.aspx?ID=117) spell that you prepared from this grimoire and that allows a saving throw, you infuse the magic with sensations of endless toil. If the target fails its saving throw against the spell, it becomes [fatigued](/Conditions.aspx?ID=15) for 1 minute by the sense of exhaustion imbued in the magic.

</column>

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Fire" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=72" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Bulk** 4

</row>

---

This bright-red _[+3 greater resilient ](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2804) [full plate](/Armor.aspx?ID=50)_ is adorned with eerily beautiful, angry flames that flow and glow with your movement, making it appear as if you are engulfed in a living fire. You gain [resistance](/Rules.aspx?ID=2312) 10 to fire while wearing this armor.

**Activate—Living Flame** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([aura](/Traits.aspx?ID=542), [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=604)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** The armor engulfs you in a vortex of living fire in a 15-foot [emanation](/Rules.aspx?ID=2387) for 10 minutes. Creatures that enter this aura or start their turn within it take 10d6 fire damage (DC 40 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2297) Reflex save). This area is [difficult terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=2366) for other creatures.

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Free Action" /><row>([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561))</row></row>

 

**Trigger** You're critically hit by a firearm attack.

 
</row>

</column>

---

This talisman usually takes the form of a small sentimental object carried in a pocket or attached to the inside of a piece of armor. When you activate it, it slows the attack, and you reduce the damage from the triggering critical hit by 10, as the attack destroys the talisman. This effect only reduces the additional damage from a critical hit; it can't reduce the damage below the amount it would deal on a normal hit.

**Source** [GM Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=218) pg. 291 **Price** 19,000 gp **Usage** worn garment **Bulk** 2 --- This strange and intricate harness fits snugly to the torso. Once you invest the apparatus, numerous artificial limbs with various tools, clamps, and lenses whirl into action, following your mental commands effortlessly.
When using this apparatus, you gain a +3 item bonus to Crafting checks to [Craft](/Actions.aspx?ID=43), [Earn Income](/Actions.aspx?ID=23), and [Repair](/Actions.aspx?ID=42), and you reduce the minimum time required to Craft an item to 1 day. If you succeed at your Crafting check and spend more downtime to continue work on the item after the minimum number of days, each day you spend reduces the remaining raw material cost by an amount based on your level + 1 and your proficiency rank in Crafting; on a critical success, each day reduces the remaining raw material cost by an amount based on your level + 2 and your proficiency rank. If you are 20th level, on a critical success your progress is 50 gp, 100 gp, 200 gp, or 350 gp for trained, expert, master, or legendary proficiency, respectively. **Activate—Inexplicable Patch** ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104)) **Frequency** once per day; **Effect** You command the apparatus to magically jury-rig an item you hold or that's within 5 feet of you. The item is repaired, as a 3rd-rank [_mending_](/Spells.aspx?ID=189) spell. This lasts for 10 minutes, after which the item returns to its previous state of disrepair unless you've Repaired it before then.

---

You regain triple the normal number of Hit Points when resting (meaning you regain triple your Constitution modifier multiplied by your level). The healing you gain from long-term rest is similarly tripled. Once per day, from any distance, Abrogail Thrune II can recite a voidability clause in your Thrune contract as a 1-minute activity to prevent you from regaining Hit Points from resting for 1 day.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> command;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You recite a subclause regarding mandatory remediation from your Thrune contract. For 6 rounds, at the start of your turn each round, you recover 25 Hit Points unless you took good damage since the start of your previous turn.

</row>

---

This elegant _+1 [striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2829) [sword cane](/Weapons.aspx?ID=400)_ serves equally well as both a fashionable accessory and a hidden weapon suitable for high-society events where weapons aren't typically permitted.

**Activate—Hide Magic** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645))    **Effect** You twist the sword cane's hilt, magically merging the blade into the cane. While the blade is merged, it can't be drawn and gains the benefits of a 3rd-rank [_disguise magic_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1491) spell to appear non-magical. Passive observers can't attempt a check to notice the cane is anything more than a mundane, if superb, fashion accessory. Those carefully examining it can discern the cane is more than it appears, but doing so is extremely difficult (DC 30 Perception). Activating the sword cane again releases the blade, allowing it to be drawn normally.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Alchemical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=6" />
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=36" />
<trait label="Elixir" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=59" />
<trait label="Polymorph" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=127" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Core Rulebook](/Sources.aspx?ID=1) pg. 548

**Price** 6 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Single Action" /><row>Interact</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

---

Favored by spies and tricksters, an infiltrator’s elixir is used to alter your appearance. When imbibed, you take the shape of a humanoid creature of your size, but different enough so you might be unrecognizable. If you aren’t a humanoid, you might take on a form more similar to your own, at the GM’s discretion.

 The creator of the elixir decides the basics of the appearance you transform into when you imbibe the elixir, including eye color, skin tone, and hair color. The elixir can’t change your form into that of a specific person. After the form takes hold, you retain it for the next 10 minutes. 

 Drinking this elixir counts as setting up a disguise to Impersonate. You gain a +4 status bonus to your Deception DC to avoid others seeing through your disguise, and you add your level to this DC even if untrained.

---

This flask contains a caustic irritant that makes a target’s skin, scales, or carapace extremely sensitive to further nicks and burns. An inflammation flask deals the listed acid damage and acid [splash](/Traits.aspx?ID=699) damage. On a hit, the target also gains [weakness](/Rules.aspx?ID=2317) to acid, fire, and slashing damage for 3 rounds. Many types of inflammation flask grant a bonus to attack rolls.

The target can end the weakness effect by three means: being drenched with water (such as submersion or exposure to an area [water](/Traits.aspx?ID=732) effect), being [Administered First Aid](/Actions.aspx?ID=2396) (whose DC in based on the bomb type), or regaining Hit Points from a single effect equal to twice the inflammation flask’s level. A creature that critically fails to Administer First Aid in this way deals untyped damage to the target equal to the inflammation flask’s initial acid damage.

---

This reservoir and spring-loaded needle can be attached to a weapon to let it inject deadly poisons. Additionally, the reservoir can be filled with an [injury](/Traits.aspx?ID=97) poison. Immediately after a successful attack with the adjusted weapon, you can inject the target with the loaded poison by activating the reservoir with an Interact action. Refilling the reservoir with a new poison requires 3 Interact actions and uses both hands.

 Adding an injection reservoir to a weapon throws off its balance, causing the multiple attack penalty with the weapon to be one greater than usual (usually –6 on a second attack and –11 on a third; or –5 and –10 with an [agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170) weapon).

Adding an injection reservoir to a weapon throws off its balance, causing the multiple attack penalty with the weapon to be one greater than usual (usually –6 on a second attack and –11 on a third; or –5 and –10 with an [agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=526) weapon).

>
[Injigo's Loving Embrace](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3147)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Season of Ghosts</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Unique" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=161" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Transmutation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=157" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #198: No Breath to Cry](/Sources.aspx?ID=224) pg. 77

**Price** 675 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 2 hands

**Bulk** 1
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This net was woven by the jorogumo Injigo, who presented it as a gift to her gnome sweetheart, Mara, to keep her safe in their mountain cottage when Injigo left on hunting expeditions.

 _Injigo's Loving Embrace_ functions as a typical [net](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2738). You gain a +1 item bonus to Athletics checks made to [Grapple](/Actions.aspx?ID=2376) with the net.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> envision, Interact;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You spin the net in the direction of an incorporeal creature within 30 feet that you can see. Lines of silken force whip out to lash around the incorporeal creature, who must attempt a DC 25 Reflex save to avoid becoming [immobilized](/Conditions.aspx?ID=81) until the end of your next turn. You can Sustain this activation for up to 1 minute, and the creature must succeed at a DC 25 check to [Escape](/Actions.aspx?ID=2296) the net.

**Activate** <actions string="" /> 10 minutes (envision, Interact);  **Frequency** once per week;   **Effect** You wrap the net around you like a blanket as you prepare to sleep. As long as you get 8 hours of sleep or analogous rest, you dream of writing love letters to someone you adore: this could be an actual paramour, someone you're interested in, or someone unknown whose identity you don't recall after waking. When you wake, you're filled with a sense of melancholia about those unsent letters, but these feelings distract you from other, more unpleasant thoughts, granting you resistance 5 to mental damage and a +1 item bonus to saving throws against mental effects for the next 8 hours.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="No Alignment" url="/Rules.aspx?ID=95" />
<trait label="Intelligent" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=280" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 194

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand or free-standing

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

**Perception** +11; [precise](/Rules.aspx?ID=411) vision 30 feet, [imprecise](/Rules.aspx?ID=412) hearing 30 feet

**Communication** speech (five languages)

**Skills** [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2) +12, [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10) +9, [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11) +10, [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13) +9, [Scribing Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) +12, [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=14) +10

**Int** +4, **Wis** +3, **Cha** +1

**Will** +11 

</column>

---        

A colorful feather adorns an _inquisitive quill_, which never runs out of ink. Essentially a Tiny construct, an _inquisitive quill_ can stand on its own when given a surface, balancing as it writes or stands. (Drawing a line gives it an effective Speed of 5 feet.) It has strong curiosity, eagerly writing any information offered to it, often acting as a scribe for its partner. The quill copies text and drawings it can see or transcribes dictation it hears. It writes at a rate that rivals that of an expert scribe.

</column>

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 6+"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Insistent Door Knocker](/Equipment.aspx?ID=511)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Conjuration" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=33" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=12) pg. 72

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** 1
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This dark iron door knocker comes in a variety of shapes, such as a bird clutching a ring in its talons or a gargoyle holding a ring in its mouth. Placing the door knocker on the surface of a door (an Interact action) causes it to attach and remain in place. While in place, the door knocker whispers hints to you while you attempt to unlock the door, granting a +1 item bonus to [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=17) checks to Pick a Lock. Removing the door knocker from a surface requires you to use an Interact action.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> command, Interact;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You place the door knocker against a wall, floor, or ceiling. The door knocker fuses in place and creates a usable door within the surface. Any creature can move through the door normally, as if the door had always been there. The door can penetrate up to 1 foot of material, so thick material, such as heavy stone walls, can cause this effect to fail, expending its use for the day. A thin layer of metal in a wall, floor, or ceiling also causes the effect to fail. You can use an Interact action to release the door knocker from the surface and return the surface to its previous shape.

</column>

>
[Inspiring Spotlight](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3531)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Convocation</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=683" />
<trait label="Light" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=640" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=644" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rival Academies](/Sources.aspx?ID=235) pg. 56, [Pathfinder #152: Legacy of the Lost God](/Sources.aspx?ID=23) pg. 73

<row gap="medium">

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

An _inspiring spotlight_ consists of a drum-shaped metal housing around several reflective plates. It has the capacity to cast a powerful, narrow beam of light to illuminate important moments or characters on stage. The portable version consists of an 18-inch-diameter lamp on a tripod that can be set up or broken down over the course of 10 minutes. The mounted version is typically 3 feet in diameter and affixed to a bracket above and behind the audience for indoor performances.

**Activate—Light It Up** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([light](/Traits.aspx?ID=640), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per hour;   **Effect** The _inspiring spotlight_ emits a 5-foot burst of bright magical light within 120 feet. If the burst intersects with an area of magical darkness, the _inspiring spotlight_ attempts to counteract the darkness with a +17 modifier. Creatures within the burst gain a +1 item bonus to saving throws and Charisma-based skill checks. The spotlight remains lit for 1 minute or until you Interact to turn it off. During this time any creature adjacent to the spotlight can move the burst up to 20 feet from the burst’s original position with an Interact action.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

<title

    right="Item 9"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[Inspiring Spotlight](/Equipment.aspx?ID=585)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Extinction Curse</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Enchantment" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=61" />
<trait label="Light" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=100" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #152: Legacy of the Lost God](/Sources.aspx?ID=23) pg. 73, [Rival Academies](/Sources.aspx?ID=235) pg. 56

**Price** 650 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 2 hands

**Bulk** 3
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

An _inspiring spotlight_ is a bulky contraption consisting of a drum-shaped metal housing around several reflective metal plates. Two handles on either side, each with a small button, allow you to aim the spotlight outward from your body.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> Interact;  **Frequency** Once per hour;   **Effect** When you push the left-hand button, the _inspiring spotlight_ emits a beam of [bright magical light](/Rules.aspx?ID=407) in a 120-foot line that hangs in the air and remains in place even if you move the spotlight. If the line passes through an area of magical darkness or targets a creature affected by magical darkness, the _inspiring spotlight_ attempts to [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) the darkness. Creatures within the line gain a +1 item bonus to saving throws and Charisma-based skill checks. In addition, creatures in the line who are [frightened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=19) reduce the value of their frightened condition by 1 at the beginning of each turn they start in the area of the line. The beam remains in place for 1 minute or until you push the right-hand button with another Interact action to extinguish the light.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>
