<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 16"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Instant Fortress](/Equipment.aspx?ID=366)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Conjuration" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=33" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Structure" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=153" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Core Rulebook](/Sources.aspx?ID=1) pg. 596

**Price** 9,300 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This metal cube is small enough to fit in your palm. Close inspection reveals fine lines in the dark gray metal, as though the cube were folded thousands of times.

**Activate** <actions string="Three Actions" /> command, Interact;     **Effect** You toss the cube on the ground, and it immediately unfolds into an adamantine fortress. 

 The fortress is 20 feet square and 30 feet high, with adamantine stairs leading up to three sets of battlements at heights of 10 feet and 20 feet and at the top. Arrow slits along the lower battlements and crenelations at the top provide standard cover to anyone within the fortress. There’s no roof, leaving an open, 10-foot-square vertical shaft through the center of the structure.

 As a magical structure, the fortress has the structure trait. Because it expands outward, the fortress can’t catch creatures inside it as a magical structure normally does. Instead, it pushes those creatures back. It can’t push a creature into a surface or hazard this way, and stops expanding if that would happen.

 The fortress has a single door in the center of one wall on the ground level, and the door appears directly in front of you when you activate the fortress. Provided you’re within 100 feet of the door, you can cause the door to open or slam shut and lock by spending a single action to issue a verbal command, which has the auditory trait. The DC to Force Open the door or Pick its Lock is 40.

 You can instantly return the _instant fortress_ to its cube form by spending a single action to issue a verbal command, which has the auditory trait. Once deactivated, the fortress can’t be activated again for 4 hours.

 If the fortress becomes damaged, it can be repaired only with a [_remake_](/Spells.aspx?ID=249) spell or by someone who is legendary at Crafting.

</column>

>
[Instant Spy](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1116)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Clockwork" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=331" />
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=36" />
<trait label="Gadget" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=405" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 70

_[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) All Pathfinder Society agents have access to all uncommon clockwork items and gadgets from Chapters 1 and 2 of this book_

**Price** 5 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

**Access** Characters from Absalom, New Thassilon, Alkenstar, Dongun Hold, or especially technological regions of Arcadia like the Deadshot Lands have access to uncommon clockwork items from the first two chapters of this book. Due to the use of technology, all gadgets are uncommon or rare, though inventors and regions with access to inventors have access to uncommon gadgets.

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Single Action" /><row>([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104))</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

An instant spy is a tiny clockwork device that is small enough to be easily hidden. It contains the same audio-recording mechanisms as a [clockwork spy](/Monsters.aspx?ID=1095), as well as a short-lived gemstone that can store up to 1 hour of sound to play back later.

 Once you have activated the instant spy, it surreptitiously begins recording all the sounds around it for an hour. In general, it can hear sounds that are clearly audible in the location where you activated it, but not sounds that would require a Perception check with a DC of 10 or greater to hear. The GM determines exactly what the instant spy can hear and record, as well as whether or not the recording is clear in a situation where the original sound is quiet, distorted, or intentionally obscured.

 When the recording is complete, once within the next 24 hours, you or another creature can use an Interact action to play back the stored audio in its entirety, after which the gem crumbles to dust. If no one plays the recorded sounds back within 1 day, the gem crumbles into dust anyway. This prevents the information from falling into the wrong hands later. It's typical to use the [Conceal an Object](/Actions.aspx?ID=61) action to hide an instant spy in a location once you've activated it, since if you don't hide it, it's relatively easy to discover in a thorough search, despite the fact that it's small and relatively unobtrusive.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 10"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Instinct Crown](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2338)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 152

**Price** 900 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn headwear

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

An _instinct crown_ is a magical headpiece imbued with the essence of instincts that [barbarians](/Classes.aspx?ID=2) draw upon in combat. Each crown is fashioned to represent the instinct it's tied to, such as a wolf's head for an [animal instinct](/Instincts.aspx?ID=1) crown or a simple helmet with Jotun runes for a [giant instinct](/Instincts.aspx?ID=4) crown. When worn, the crown allows you to tap further into your instincts, granting you even greater benefits if the crown's essence matches your instinct. You must be able to [Rage](/Actions.aspx?ID=3) to use the crown's activations.

**Activate** <actions string="Free Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** You roll initiative; **Requirements** You have [Quick-Tempered](/Actions.aspx?ID=2803) and meet its requirements;; **Effect** You use Quick-Tempered and gain 10 additional temporary Hit Points from your Rage.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [rage](/Traits.aspx?ID=680)) **Frequency** once per day;  **Requirements** You’re raging, and the crown’s instinct matches your barbarian instinct; **Effect** You draw upon your instinct to gain a boon, as follows. 

_Animal:_ Your bestial instincts take over, granting you greater ferocity. You can Stride as part of the activation, and you gain 10 additional temporary Hit Points from your rage. Until the end of your rage, you deal 3 additional damage with your animal’s unarmed attacks, and those unarmed attacks gain the [deadly](/Traits.aspx?ID=570) d8 trait. 

_Dragon:_ The might of dragons surrounds you in the form of dancing flames, poisonous wisps, or another appropriate manifestation. Until the end of your rage, adjacent creatures that hit you with a melee attack, as well as creatures that touch you or hit you with an unarmed attack, take 2d6 damage each time they do. The damage type is that of your instinct’s dragon breath. 

_Fury:_ Your boundless fury allows you push past your natural limits, moving with unmatched speed. You become [quickened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=89) until the end of your rage. You can use your extra action only to [Stride](/Actions.aspx?ID=2305) or [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306). 

_Giant:_ If you have the space to do so and aren’t already, you become Large. Your equipment grows with you but returns to its natural size if removed. Increase your reach by 5 feet (or by 10 feet if you were Tiny). You deal 2 additional damage when using your larger weapon. Also, when you Stride along the ground, you can shatter the earth with your footfalls, and any squares you move through become [difficult terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=2366). You ignore the difficult terrain you create. The ground reverts to normal when your rage ends. 

_Spirit:_ You take on the partial form of a spirit, becoming somewhat incorporeal. Your raging resistance applies to all physical damage and poison damage, although you halve this resistance against magical attacks. 

_Superstition:_ Your body fights off the effects of magic with even greater effect. Until the end of your rage, when you attempt a saving throw against magic, roll twice and take the higher result. This is a [fortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=612) effect. Also, your raging resistance applies to all magic traditions while you rage.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

fields.text: Item 10 Instinct Crown Invested Magical Transmutation Source Treasure Vault pg. 152 Price 900 gp Usage worn headwear Bulk L An instinct crown is a magical headpiece imbued with the essence of instincts that barbarians draw upon in combat. Each crown is fashioned to represent the instinct it’s tied to, such as a wolf’s head for an animal instinct crown or a simple helmet with Jotun runes for a giant instinct crown . When worn, the crown allows you to tap further into your instincts, granting you even greater benefits if the crown’s essence matches your instinct. You must be able to Rage to use the crown’s activations. Activate Free Action envision; Trigger You roll initiative; Effect You Rage, gaining 10 additional temporary Hit Points. Activate Two Actions command, envision; Requirements The crown’s instinct matches your barbarian instinct; Effect You Rage and draw upon your instinct to gain a boon, as follows. Animal: Your bestial instincts take over, granting you greater ferocity. You can Stride as part of the activation, and you gain 10 additional temporary Hit Points. Until the end of your rage, you deal 3 additional damage with your animal’s unarmed attacks, and those unarmed attacks gain the deadly d8 trait. Dragon: The might of dragons surrounds you in the form of dancing flames, whirling ice, or another appropriate manifestation. Until the end of your rage, adjacent creatures that hit you with a melee attack, as well as creatures that touch you or hit you with an unarmed attack, take 2d6 damage each time they do. The damage type is that of your dragon’s breath weapon. Fury: Your boundless fury allows you push past your natural limits, moving with unmatched speed. You become quickened until the end of your rage. You can use your extra action only to Stride or Strike. Giant: If you have the space to do so and aren’t already, you become Large. Your equipment grows with you but returns to its natural size if removed. Increase your reach by 5 feet (or by 10 feet if you were Tiny). You deal 2 additional damage when using your larger weapon. Also, when you Stride along the ground, you can shatter the earth with your footfalls, and any squares you move through become difficult terrain. You ignore the difficult terrain you create. The ground reverts to normal when your rage ends. Spirit: You take on the partial form of a spirit, becoming somewhat incorporeal. Your raging resistance applies to all physical damage and poison damage, although you halve this resistance against magical attacks. Superstition: Your body fights off the effects of magic with even greater effect. Until the end of your rage, when you attempt a saving throw against magic, roll twice and take the higher result. This is a fortune effect. Also, your raging resistance applies to all magic traditions while you rage.

Many armies recruit musicians among their number, who might keep time for marching with a drum, play out commands with a bugle, or intimidate foes with the bagpipes. Regardless of instrument, these musicians are still soldiers and need to be able to fight as well as play at the drop of a hat. The _instrument harness_ is made from white leather decorated with gold musical symbols. You can attach up to 3 Bulk of musical instruments to the harness. If you drop an attached instrument, it remains safely at your side rather than dropped to the ground.

**Activate—Ready to Play** <actions string="Free Action" /> ;  **Frequency** once per day;  **Requirements** There is an instrument attached to the _instrument harness_ and you have enough hands free to hold it; **Effect** Your harness ripples, pulling the required instrument into your hands. You [Interact](/Actions.aspx?ID=2297) to draw the required instrument, but this [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645) action doesn’t trigger reactions.

---

Inubrix is much softer than steel, and it's atypical for it to be used to make shields. An item made by an unskilled smith will dent from a single blow and prove worthless on the battlefield. However, its yielding surface can entrap metal weapons. You can use an inubrix shield (or [shield boss](/Weapons.aspx?ID=41) or [shield spikes](/Weapons.aspx?ID=42) on an inubrix shield) to [Disarm](/Actions.aspx?ID=41) a metal item with the [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) skill even if you don't have a free hand; doing so uses the weapon's reach (if different from your own) and adds the weapon's item bonus to attack rolls (if any) as an item bonus to the Athletics check. If you critically fail a check to Disarm a metal item using the weapon, you can drop the weapon to take the effects of a failure instead of a critical failure. On a critical success, you still need a free hand if you want to take the item.

---

Inubrix is much softer than steel, and it's atypical for it to be used to make shields. An item made by an unskilled smith will dent from a single blow and prove worthless on the battlefield. However, its yielding surface can entrap metal weapons. You can use an inubrix shield (or [shield boss](/Weapons.aspx?ID=41) or [shield spikes](/Weapons.aspx?ID=42) on an inubrix shield) to [Disarm](/Actions.aspx?ID=41) a metal item with the [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) skill even if you don't have a free hand; doing so uses the weapon's reach (if different from your own) and adds the weapon's item bonus to attack rolls (if any) as an item bonus to the Athletics check. If you critically fail a check to Disarm a metal item using the weapon, you can drop the weapon to take the effects of a failure instead of a critical failure. On a critical success, you still need a free hand if you want to take the item.

[Inubrix Shield](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1417)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Grand Bazaar](/Sources.aspx?ID=100) pg. 99

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** varies by shield

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

**Base Material** [Inubrix](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1415)

</column>

---

Inubrix is much softer than steel, and it's atypical for it to be used to make shields. An item made by an unskilled smith will dent from a single blow and prove worthless on the battlefield. However, its yielding surface can entrap metal weapons. You can use an inubrix shield (or [shield boss](/Weapons.aspx?ID=41) or [shield spikes](/Weapons.aspx?ID=42) on an inubrix shield) to [Disarm](/Actions.aspx?ID=41) a metal item with the [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) skill even if you don't have a free hand; doing so uses the weapon's reach (if different from your own) and adds the weapon's item bonus to attack rolls (if any) as an item bonus to the Athletics check. If you critically fail a check to Disarm a metal item using the weapon, you can drop the weapon to take the effects of a failure instead of a critical failure. On a critical success, you still need a free hand if you want to take the item.

</title>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Grand Bazaar](/Sources.aspx?ID=100) pg. 99

**Bulk**  varies by weapon
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

**Base Material** [Inubrix](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1415)

</column>

---

While inubrix weapons don't pack the same punch as more durable weapons, they have the unique ability to bypass some of the protections offered by metal armors and shields. A weapon crafted from inubrix reduces the weapon's damage die by 1 size. However, they ignore the resistance to damage from metal armor's armor specialization effects and the circumstance bonus to AC from metal shields. Strikes with inubrix weapons don't trigger the [Shield Block](/Feats.aspx?ID=839) reaction from a metal shield. Weapons that normally deal 1d4 damage can't be crafted from inubrix.

The chair comes equipped with [wheel blades](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1363), and portions of its frame contain [sterling artisan's tools](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3). The _inventor's chair_ might be a family heirloom or a gift from someone who inherited it. It could instead sit unused in its inventor's abandoned estate, awaiting another user. --- **Minor Gifts**: [emotion surge](/Relics.aspx?ID=92), [muse](/Relics.aspx?ID=87) ([Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=4))
**Major Gifts**: [emotion conduit](/Relics.aspx?ID=94), [enthralling](/Relics.aspx?ID=89)
**Grand Gift**: [artistic perfection](/Relics.aspx?ID=90) (Crafting)

---

Some [inventors](/Classes.aspx?ID=19) in Tian Xia put fried snacks near their innovations, a charm to make devices behave as intended. The practice rubbed off on other inventors, who replaced the food with a drawing on an _inventor's fulu_. When you Activate the fulu, your critical failure becomes a failure, and you can spend just 1 minute to return your innovation to full functionality. The fulu then burns up, and its effects end.

    pfs="Limited"
>
[Invigorating Soap](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3139)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Season of Ghosts</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Alchemical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=6" />
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=36" />
<trait label="Healing" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=89" />
<trait label="Processed" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=487" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #197: Let the Leaves Fall](/Sources.aspx?ID=222) pg. 74

**Price** 28 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="" /><row>10 minutes (Interact)</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This slender bar of pine-scented soap can only be activated when you're immersed in water. Upon activation, the soap covers you in a sudsy foam that quickly fades, filling you with energy and soothing away aches and pains. It immediately restores 10 Hit Points and removes the fatigued condition. If you begin an 8-hour period of rest immediately after using invigorating soap, you regain an additional 10 Hit Points from resting.

---

This _+2 [resilient](/Equipment.aspx?ID=279) [invisibility](/Equipment.aspx?ID=287) [chain shirt](/Armor.aspx?ID=6)_ is itself invisible. Other creatures can't see it at all, allowing you to wear it surreptitiously. Additionally, the armor's invisible composition is quieter and more comfortable than a normal chain shirt. It loses the [noisy](/Traits.aspx?ID=205) trait and gains the [comfort](/Traits.aspx?ID=203) trait.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> envision;  **Frequency** once per minute;   **Effect** You Stride and turn partially invisible, becoming [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=4) until the end of your next turn or until you use a [hostile action](/Rules.aspx?ID=300), whichever comes first. As normal, you can use the concealment from this activation to [Hide](/Actions.aspx?ID=62).

    pfs="Standard"
>
[Iris of the Sky](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1182)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Unique" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=161" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 165

**Price** 240 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 2 hands

**Bulk** 2
</row>

<row gap="medium">
**Base Weapon** [Jezail](/Weapons.aspx?ID=203)
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This _+1 striking [jezail](/Weapons.aspx?ID=203)_ is built from white hot metal and has a ruby fused into the palm wood stock. When the _iris of the sky_ misfires, you take 5 [persistent fire damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29).

 The first firearm of this type came as the result of a gunslinger who entreated an [efreeti](/Monsters.aspx?ID=214), wishing for the might of the desert sun. The weapon constantly glows and burns with a brilliant intensity. The firearm has since belonged to an extensive string of users and been replicated several times, though each wielder of the weapon, whether the original or one of its copies, has eventually ended up as a charred husk, slain by fire in battle or unusual accidents that no one could quite explain except, perhaps, the efreet.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per minute;   **Effect** You focus the solar energy housed in the ruby to release a gout of solar flame instead of a bullet. Make a Strike with the _iris of the sky_. All damage from this Strike is fire damage and the target takes an additional 1d6 fire damage and 1d6 persistent fire damage.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645), [fortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=612)) **Frequency** once per minute;   **Effect** You make a wish into the _iris of the sky_, yearning for it to strike true, and then fire. Strike against a foe with the iris, rolling the attack roll twice and taking the better result. If the attack is a failure, you take 5 persistent fire damage.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

This hearty meat-and-potato stew has an unusual shine to it and seems to sparkle when it catches the right light. That's because it's been infused with a specially treated iron dust, which Sanra Copperstone promises will strengthen the bones and make for healthier skin. Eating this delicious, if metallic, stew adds that same sheen to your own skin, while also hardening it. You gain 3 resistance to physical damage for 1 minute, but take a –2 item penalty to [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) and [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) checks during that time.

When you crack open this soft, spongy seedpod, you can use it as a [catalyst](/Rules.aspx?ID=1509) when casting a [_mist_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1606) spell. When you do, irritating pollen fills the area for the spell’s duration. Creatures in the area must attempt a Fortitude saving throw at the listed DC to avoid sneezing uncontrollably. On a failed save, the creature gains the listed condition for the listed time. A creature that succeeds at this saving throw becomes temporarily immune to the irritating seedpod’s pollen for 10 minutes.

May contain spoilers from Bastion of Blasphemies **Source** [Pathfinder #224: Bastion of Blasphemies](/Sources.aspx?ID=357) pg. 235 **Usage** held in 1 hand **Bulk** 1 --- Each _Arudora memento_ is unique in appearance, but all seven are approximately the same size. Carried by each of the cursed family members, these mementos have within them the power to unlock entire portions of Bastardhall from the ghostly cursed state the castle traditionally exists in. Each of the seven mementos has the following activation, but the section of castle unlocked by each activation, as well as each memento’s specific benefit granted to the PCs, varies by type. **Activate—Return Memento** ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Effect** You place the memento into the appropriate statue’s clutches in the fountain located in area
**B3** of Bastardhall. The statue briefly animates to claim the memento, which turns to stone and becomes thereafter a permanent part of the statue, effectively destroying the memento while granting a boon to the party that persists for the remainder of this Adventure Path. A section of Bastardhall solidifies from its ghostly form, unlocking its reaches for the PCs to explore. **Destruction** An _Arudora memento_ is destroyed when it’s activated with Return Memento, and the boon it grants upon this returning lasts until the very end of the Adventure Path. Alisendra's Fan **Source** [Pathfinder #224: Bastion of Blasphemies](/Sources.aspx?ID=357) pg. 235 **Bulk** L --- When this elegant crimson hand fan is Returned, the dungeon (detailed in Chapter 5) is unlocked. The souls trapped in Bastardhall appreciate the end of Alisendra’s dominion and now whisper hints of truths in the ears of those who seek knowledge. The DCs for all checks made to [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=2367) are reduced by 1 for the rest of the Adventure Path. Augsten's Cudgel **Source** [Pathfinder #224: Bastion of Blasphemies](/Sources.aspx?ID=357) pg. 235 **Bulk** L --- When this bloodstained wooden cudgel is Returned, the reception halls (detailed in Chapter 4) are unlocked. Sometimes, violence is the only answer, and swift action to combat is rewarded. For the rest of the Adventure Path, all PCs gain a +1 bonus to any initiative rolls; this special bonus combines with all other bonuses. Dazerien's Thumbscrew **Source** [Pathfinder #224: Bastion of Blasphemies](/Sources.aspx?ID=357) pg. 235 **Bulk** L --- When this gory bronze thumbscrew is Returned, the private halls (detailed in Chapter 6) are unlocked. Rest becomes more rewarding now that the sadist of the dungeon has been defeated. For the rest of the Adventure Path, when the PCs take their 8-hour period of rest, they recover an additional number of Hit Points equal to their Constitution modifier (minimum 1) times their level. Irrokcis's Medallion **Source** [Pathfinder #224: Bastion of Blasphemies](/Sources.aspx?ID=357) pg. 235 **Bulk** L --- When this eerie medallion is Returned, the towers (detailed in Chapter 9) are unlocked, and the spirits of those trapped in Bastardhall rise up to aid the PCs. All weapon Strikes made by PCs deal an additional 1 spirit damage for the rest of the Adventure Path. Jinnivere's Riding Crop **Source** [Pathfinder #224: Bastion of Blasphemies](/Sources.aspx?ID=357) pg. 235 **Bulk** L --- When this leather riding crop is Returned, the cellars (detailed in Chapter 3) are unlocked. Companions are now more hearty and full of life—PC companions (such as familiars, eidolons, and animal companions) gain a +1 status bonus to all saving throws for the remainder of this Adventure Path. Raudltz's Telescope **Source** [Pathfinder #224: Bastion of Blasphemies](/Sources.aspx?ID=357) pg. 235 **Bulk** L --- When this handheld telescope is Returned, the fallen temple (detailed in Chapter 7) is unlocked. Secrets are now more difficult to hide in Bastardhall. Reduce all Perception DCs made when [Seeking](/Actions.aspx?ID=2301) or [Searching](/Actions.aspx?ID=2630) by 2 for the rest of this Adventure Path. Ryhasphinea's Hourglass **Source** [Pathfinder #224: Bastion of Blasphemies](/Sources.aspx?ID=357) pg. 235 **Bulk** L --- When this cracked hourglass is Returned, the vaults (detailed in Chapter 8) are unlocked. Death’s grasp on the PCs wanes—for the rest of this Adventure Path, the DCs for all recovery checks made by a [dying](/Conditions.aspx?ID=69) PC are reduced by 2.

[Item Cache](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2470)
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Firebrands](/Sources.aspx?ID=196) pg. 93

<row gap="medium">

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Item caches serve as places where you can pick up supplies, and suppliers are the people or organizations who provide the items and locations for these caches. This service is useful for scheduling a quick resupply of food along a specified route during a long journey, or for setting up specific items that need to be accessed at an appointed time and place, such as having a cache of weapons accessible to an infiltration party behind enemy lines. On popular travel routes, Firebrands and other adventuring groups have regular access points where they can easily set up a resource drop, thanks to suppliers who are typically supportive locals and who make a small income off running supplies to drop locations.

 Cached items carry an automatic 10% markup in addition to a flat fee determined by the rarity and Bulk of the items in total. The price of the cache includes the cost of sourcing the items requested. The maximum item level available for cached items is typically equal to the maximum allowed by the level of the city or settlement. [Extradimensional](/Traits.aspx?ID=67) spaces such as [bags of holding](/Equipment.aspx?ID=249) can be used for item caches, and the cost of those specialized containers must be paid in advance. The GM decides if you can commission the services of a supplier who can set up an item cache and what items can be sourced for that particular cache.

 Common item caches take 1d6 days to prepare and secure, while uncommon item caches take 1d6 months to prepare and secure due to the volatility of the market— there is no guarantee that a specific uncommon item can be found, even for professionals who have connections with the right networks. The extended time required to locate uncommon items factors into the cost of uncommon item caches. Regardless of the rarity of the items contained, level 1 item caches can hold up to 5 Bulk, level 2 item caches can hold up to 10 Bulk, level 3 item caches can hold up to 25 Bulk, and level 4 item caches can hold up to 50 Bulk. Caches larger than 50 Bulk draw too much attention and must either be broken up into multiple smaller caches or be arranged as alternate deliveries, such as a shipment to a local and trusted warehouse. If you are supplying all the items for an item cache, you need only to pay the flat fee for a common item cache of the appropriate level for the Bulk contained, regardless of the rarity of the items being held in the cache.

Item caches serve as places where you can pick up supplies, and suppliers are the people or organizations who provide the items and locations for these caches. This service is useful for scheduling a quick resupply of food along a specified route during a long journey, or for setting up specific items that need to be accessed at an appointed time and place, such as having a cache of weapons accessible to an infiltration party behind enemy lines. On popular travel routes, Firebrands and other adventuring groups have regular access points where they can easily set up a resource drop, thanks to suppliers who are typically supportive locals and who make a small income off running supplies to drop locations.

 Cached items carry an automatic 10% markup in addition to a flat fee determined by the rarity and Bulk of the items in total. The price of the cache includes the cost of sourcing the items requested. The maximum item level available for cached items is typically equal to the maximum allowed by the level of the city or settlement. [Extradimensional](/Traits.aspx?ID=67) spaces such as [bags of holding](/Equipment.aspx?ID=249) can be used for item caches, and the cost of those specialized containers must be paid in advance. The GM decides if you can commission the services of a supplier who can set up an item cache and what items can be sourced for that particular cache.

 Common item caches take 1d6 days to prepare and secure, while uncommon item caches take 1d6 months to prepare and secure due to the volatility of the market— there is no guarantee that a specific uncommon item can be found, even for professionals who have connections with the right networks. The extended time required to locate uncommon items factors into the cost of uncommon item caches. Caches larger than 50 Bulk draw too much attention and must either be broken up into multiple smaller caches or be arranged as alternate deliveries, such as a shipment to a local and trusted warehouse. If you are supplying all the items for an item cache, you need only to pay the flat fee for a common item cache of the appropriate level for the Bulk contained, regardless of the rarity of the items being held in the cache.

 Common item caches take 1d6 days to prepare and secure, while uncommon item caches take 1d6 months to prepare and secure due to the volatility of the market— there is no guarantee that a specific uncommon item can be found, even for professionals who have connections with the right networks. The extended time required to locate uncommon items factors into the cost of uncommon item caches. Regardless of the rarity of the items contained, level 1 item caches can hold up to 5 Bulk, level 2 item caches can hold up to 10 Bulk, level 3 item caches can hold up to 25 Bulk, and level 4 item caches can hold up to 50 Bulk. Caches larger than 50 Bulk draw too much attention and must either be broken up into multiple smaller caches or be arranged as alternate deliveries, such as a shipment to a local and trusted warehouse. If you are supplying all the items for an item cache, you need only to pay the flat fee for a common item cache of the appropriate level for the Bulk contained, regardless of the rarity of the items being held in the cache.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Enchantment" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=61" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Monsters of Myth](/Sources.aspx?ID=107) pg. 125

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** 1
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This white, slender rod bears intricately carved reliefs of magnificent animals that bow and dance to some unseen commander. The baton enables you to command [constructs](/Traits.aspx?ID=35).

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> command, Interact ([enchantment](/Traits.aspx?ID=61), [incapacitation](/Traits.aspx?ID=93)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You take control of a construct. This has the effects of [_dominate_](/Spells.aspx?ID=87) with a DC of 30, but it affects only constructs. It lacks the [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106) trait and functions on [mindless](/Traits.aspx?ID=108) constructs. It also ignores any [golem antimagic](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=57) the target might have. The effect's duration ends if the baton is destroyed or leaves your possession for at least 1 minute, and you can issue commands to the target only while holding the baton.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> Interact;  **Frequency** once per round;   **Effect** You closely direct the actions of one construct you control and can see within 60 feet. That construct gains a +1 status bonus to attack rolls, damage rolls, and saving throws (except saving throws against the _ivory baton_).

</title>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #171: Hurricane's Howl](/Sources.aspx?ID=101) pg. 76

**Price** 150 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** affixed to headgear

</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Free Action" /><row>envision</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Via some strange alchemical reaction with the gasses of Terwa Lake, the [cloud dragon](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=176) Ixamè's eyeballs have shriveled into sky-blue gems. The dragon's sense of vision isn't impaired, and her eyes can't be removed from her head until she's destroyed. Once removed, each gem functions as a special talisman. _Ixamè's eye_ sparkles when it's in an area of fog or mist. Activating the talisman enables you to see clearly through fog and mist for 1 minute; any creature [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=4) only by fog or mist is no longer concealed to you. If such a creature was relying on the concealment to [Hide](/Actions.aspx?ID=62) or [Sneak](/Actions.aspx?ID=63), this also means it's no longer [hidden](/Conditions.aspx?ID=22) or [undetected](/Conditions.aspx?ID=39).

[Jaathoom's Scarf](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2582)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Air" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=5" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 75

**Price** 900 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn belt

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This scarf is made of fine silk that's the same shade of blue as a clear, cloudless sky. The short ends are edged with a fine gold fringe that seems to sway even in still weather as though touched by invisible winds. The long edges have exquisite embroidery in threads that vary from a blue identical to the silk to the deep gray of storm clouds during winter. Wearing this scarf grants a +2 item bonus to [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=12) checks to dance and to [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) checks to [Escape](/Actions.aspx?ID=79).

**Activate—Vanish** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** The scarf casts 4th-rank [_invisibility_](/Spells.aspx?ID=164) on you.

**Activate—Jaathoom's Rebuke** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32)) **Frequency** once per hour;   **Effect** You let the winds around you catch the edges of the _jaathoom's scarf_, and a jaathoom shuyookh appears with a sudden updraft. The winds force your enemies back, granting you some breathing room in battle. Each enemy in a 10-foot emanation must succeed at a DC 27 Fortitude save or be [pushed](/Rules.aspx?ID=451) 10 feet. A creature that critically fails is also knocked [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=31) after being moved. Creatures with the [air](/Traits.aspx?ID=5) trait are immune to all these effects.

</column>

**Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 99 **Price** 1,800 gp **Usage** held in 1 hand --- _Jabali's dice_ are two six-sided dice carved from evenly weighted stone to the specifications of a specific jabali shuyookh. The sides showing a 6 also have the name and title of the shuyookh inscribed in Petran. If you whisper the name and title during a dice game using _jabali's dice_, they bless you with a bit of luck, granting a +2 item bonus to your [Games Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) check. You can do so frequently enough to apply this bonus while [Earning Income](/Actions.aspx?ID=23) using Games Lore, but only one user at a time can do so. **Activate—Jabali's Gamble** ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104)) **Frequency** once per day; **Effect** You call out the shuyookh's name and title, then roll the dice. The shuyookh appears briefly to provide for your defense. Roll 2d6 to determine the effect. Represented by the GM, the shuyookh chooses any effect's specifications, benefiting you according to the shuyookh's whims.
**2–5**The shuyookh casts [_mountain resilience_](/Spells.aspx?ID=312) on you.
**6–9**The shuyookh casts [_grasping earth_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1334), but you and your allies are immune to it.
**10–11**The shuyookh casts [_wall of stone_](/Spells.aspx?ID=365). The edges can pass through creatures, which are shunted to the side of the wall opposite that edge.
**12**The shuyookh casts a DC 31 [_petrify_](/Spells.aspx?ID=123) spell on a creature hostile and in proximity to you. If no appealing target exists, you receive a 10–11 result instead.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Artifact" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=253" />

<column gap="tiny">

<row gap="medium">

</row>

<row gap="medium">

</column>

---

This enormous stone glows with a pale light and emits a quiet hum. Each _Jahan waystone_ is part of a paired link. The paired stones correspond in the color of the light they emit, as well as the specific tone at which they hum.

**Activate** <actions string="" /> 1 minute (envision, Interact);     **Effect** You place your hand on the stone and focus on the stone's light. The stone's glow envelopes all creatures in a 10-foot radius with its light and attempts to teleport the creatures to its paired stone. If there is no open space within 30 feet of the target waystone, the teleportation attempt fails. A creature can resist the teleportation with a successful DC 45 Will save.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 9"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Jann's Prism](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2655)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 224

**Price** 700 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Light always seems to be refracting through this simple prism, creating a hazy multicolor aura that surrounds the glass. When exposed to direct sunlight, the prism radiates a beam of light that shifts in color. This beam spells out the name of the jann shuyookh for whom the prism was designed. While holding the prism to your eye, your vision becomes overwhelmed with colors that guide your eye, granting you a +2 item bonus to visual Perception checks. If you look through the prism while you Seek, you can scan or search an area twice as large as normal (a 60-foot cone, 30-foot burst, or 20-foot square) as the varying colors help you distinguish between your surroundings.

**Activate—Jann's Light** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You raise the prism above your head and call upon the jann shuyookh to come to your aid. The shuyookh's face becomes visible in a reflection in the prism and light shines out from the prism, surrounding you in a multitude of colors. For 1 minute, you shed [bright light](/Rules.aspx?ID=407) in a 20-foot emanation (and [dim light](/Rules.aspx?ID=408) for the next 20 feet). The light coruscates with two colors chosen by the jann, and you gain resistance 5 to two damage types based on the colors chosen: **red** [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=72), **orange** [acid](/Traits.aspx?ID=3), **yellow** [electricity](/Traits.aspx?ID=56), **green** [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=126), **blue** [sonic](/Traits.aspx?ID=147), **indigo** [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106), or **violet** [force](/Traits.aspx?ID=75).

</column>

---

The teeth that fell off the [_Mantle of the Grogrisant_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1476) were given to the scholars of Houses Fahlspar, Lotheed, Nicodemius, and Zespire, who—after much heated discussion—created this regal circlet. You gain a +3 item bonus to [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) and [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) skill checks and [Sense Motive](/Actions.aspx?ID=2302) checks against creatures that have the [primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=676) trait. When you invest in the headband, you either increase your Wisdom modifier by 1 or increase it to +4, whichever would give you a higher value.

**Activate—Primal Empathy** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647)) **Frequency** once per hour;   **Effect** You gain the ability to communicate with nature as if you were a part of it. You cast [_telepathy_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1719) at 6th rank, which can only be used to communicate with creatures that have the [primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=676) trait.

</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Outlaws of Alkenstar</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Unique" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=161" />
<trait label="LN" url="/Rules.aspx?ID=95" />

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #179: Cradle of Quartz](/Sources.aspx?ID=122) pg. 77

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 2 hands

**Bulk** 1
</row>

<row gap="medium">

</row>

<row gap="medium">

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

**Perception** +13; precise vision 30 feet, imprecise hearing 30 feet

**Communication** empathy

**Skills** [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) +14, [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=16) +16

**Int** +1, **Wis** +5, **Cha** +3

**Will** +18 

</column>

---        

Jax was a caravan guard who died defending her charges from a pack of Lamashtan cultists in the Spellscar Desert. Her spirit of fury and hopelessness infused her weapon upon her death, imbuing the firearm with a fragment of her soul and intelligence. The rifle, upon awakening, remembered just enough of Jax's former life to think of her former wielder's name as her own.

 _Jax_ is a _+1 [striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=280) [fearsome](/Equipment.aspx?ID=731) [piercing wind](/Weapons.aspx?ID=221)_ whose driving purpose is to protect innocent travelers in the Spellscar Desert from raiders, bandits, and cultists. _Jax_ allows any creature to wield her, but she doesn't reveal her intelligence or powers until she detects an innocent in danger or if her wielder has proven themselves a worthy champion of justice. If she deems a wielder to be unworthy, _Jax_ uses her [_dominate_](/Spells.aspx?ID=87) ability to control the wielder until she can find a new one.

 If ever used to attack an innocent traveler, or if, in _Jax's_ opinion, the attack could be considered banditry, the weapon automatically misfires. If _Jax_ witnesses an innocent harmed or killed, she empathically urges her wielder to avenge the victim. If the wielder doesn't comply, _Jax_ attempts to cast _dominate_ (below). Even if the _dominate_ spell fails, Jax withholds all magical abilities, including the _+1 weapon potency_ rune and _striking_ rune, until her wielder redeems themself.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> command;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** _Jax_ casts [_heroism_](/Spells.aspx?ID=149) on you.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> command;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** _Jax_ deems you an unworthy agent of justice. She casts [_dominate_](/Spells.aspx?ID=87) on you (DC 24). If you're chaotic or a worshipper of [Lamashtu](/Deities.aspx?ID=11), you take a –2 penalty to your Will save, and the result of your save is one degree of success worse than the result you rolled. _Jax_ orders you to fight banditry and protect innocent travelers in the Spellscar Desert, renewing the spell as often as necessary until you cease your lawless ways.

</column>

These bioluminescent jellyfish are as bright as candles, come in a variety of colors, and can act as living lanterns. They dry up and die if removed from the water for more than 1 hour, but as long as they’re allowed access to seawater, they can usually survive for up to 1 year by feeding on micronutrients. Rarely, a well-treated jellyfish lamp might live longer and potentially develop stronger light or additional abilities.

</title>

<traits>

<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=644" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Tian Xia Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=230) pg. 129

**Price** 3,000 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">
**Base Weapon** [Longsword](/Weapons.aspx?ID=386)
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This +[2](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2830) [greater striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2829) [longsword](/Weapons.aspx?ID=386) sports no extravagant characteristics save for a blade of pure, unblemished ivory and a hilt of unmarred obsidian. It takes on the propensity of its user, turning whiter or darker based on their actions. 

The effects of life's duality are based on the number and type of charges it has. It begins with 0 charges and can gain either dark or light charges, up to a maximum of 3 charges of one type. A charge dissipates after 10 minutes or when a charge of the opposite type is gained. If you have a charge of one type and would gain the opposite type of charge, you lose your current charges. 

Life's duality gains a dark charge when it critically succeeds at a [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) against an opponent or reduces the Hit Points of a living enemy to 0. For each dark charge it has, it deals an additional 1d4 [void](/Traits.aspx?ID=510) damage (maximum 3d4). 

Life's duality gains a light charge when you use a spell, skill check, or ability to restore at least 10 Hit Points to an ally. The damage healed must have been inflicted by a significant foe or threat. For each light charge it has, you gain 1d4 temporary Hit Points at the end of each round (maximum 3d4).

**Activate—Burst of Duality** <actions string="Three Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561))   **Requirements** Life’s duality has 3 dark charges or 3 light charges; Frequency once per day; **Effect** You unleash the sword’s charged energy in a magical display. You cast a 3-action 5th-rank [_harm_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1552) spell if you have 3 dark charges or a 3-action 5th-rank [_heal_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1554) spell if you have 3 light charges (DC 30). The sword then reverts to having 0 charges.

</column>

This ornate handbell creates a sonorous low-pitched tone when rung, as if sounding from a much larger bell than one carried in the hand. The bell is crafted of silver and polished to a reflective sheen, while the bell's wooden handle is carved with detailed images of various foodstuffs. 

You can interact with a _jiang-shi_ bell to brandish it against a [jiang-shi vampire](/Monsters.aspx?ID=1909). If a _jiang-shi_ gains the fleeing condition as a result of a jiang-shi bell being brandished, they must run until they're at least 20 feet away. They take a -2 penalty to the Will save to any attempt to overcome their revulsion toward this object. 

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> envsion, Interact ([olfactory](/Traits.aspx?ID=664), [visual](/Traits.aspx?ID=727)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You ring the bell and create an illusory image of a delicious-looking banquet of food laid out on an altar in a 5-foot-square at any point within 30 feet of you that you can see. Any creature that must eat food to survive that's within 30 feet of the appearance of the illusory food must succeed at a DC 28 Will save or be so distracted by the food's sight and smell that they become fascinated by it for 10 minutes.

 This food's appearance can trigger any jiang-shi's Bitter Epiphany weakness; if the food does so, the jiang-shi takes a –2 item penalty to its Will save to resist the effects of this weakness.

May contain spoilers from Bastion of Blasphemies **Source** [Pathfinder #224: Bastion of Blasphemies](/Sources.aspx?ID=357) pg. 235 **Usage** held in 1 hand **Bulk** 1 --- Each _Arudora memento_ is unique in appearance, but all seven are approximately the same size. Carried by each of the cursed family members, these mementos have within them the power to unlock entire portions of Bastardhall from the ghostly cursed state the castle traditionally exists in. Each of the seven mementos has the following activation, but the section of castle unlocked by each activation, as well as each memento’s specific benefit granted to the PCs, varies by type. **Activate—Return Memento** ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Effect** You place the memento into the appropriate statue’s clutches in the fountain located in area
**B3** of Bastardhall. The statue briefly animates to claim the memento, which turns to stone and becomes thereafter a permanent part of the statue, effectively destroying the memento while granting a boon to the party that persists for the remainder of this Adventure Path. A section of Bastardhall solidifies from its ghostly form, unlocking its reaches for the PCs to explore. **Destruction** An _Arudora memento_ is destroyed when it’s activated with Return Memento, and the boon it grants upon this returning lasts until the very end of the Adventure Path. Alisendra's Fan **Source** [Pathfinder #224: Bastion of Blasphemies](/Sources.aspx?ID=357) pg. 235 **Bulk** L --- When this elegant crimson hand fan is Returned, the dungeon (detailed in Chapter 5) is unlocked. The souls trapped in Bastardhall appreciate the end of Alisendra’s dominion and now whisper hints of truths in the ears of those who seek knowledge. The DCs for all checks made to [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=2367) are reduced by 1 for the rest of the Adventure Path. Augsten's Cudgel **Source** [Pathfinder #224: Bastion of Blasphemies](/Sources.aspx?ID=357) pg. 235 **Bulk** L --- When this bloodstained wooden cudgel is Returned, the reception halls (detailed in Chapter 4) are unlocked. Sometimes, violence is the only answer, and swift action to combat is rewarded. For the rest of the Adventure Path, all PCs gain a +1 bonus to any initiative rolls; this special bonus combines with all other bonuses. Dazerien's Thumbscrew **Source** [Pathfinder #224: Bastion of Blasphemies](/Sources.aspx?ID=357) pg. 235 **Bulk** L --- When this gory bronze thumbscrew is Returned, the private halls (detailed in Chapter 6) are unlocked. Rest becomes more rewarding now that the sadist of the dungeon has been defeated. For the rest of the Adventure Path, when the PCs take their 8-hour period of rest, they recover an additional number of Hit Points equal to their Constitution modifier (minimum 1) times their level. Irrokcis's Medallion **Source** [Pathfinder #224: Bastion of Blasphemies](/Sources.aspx?ID=357) pg. 235 **Bulk** L --- When this eerie medallion is Returned, the towers (detailed in Chapter 9) are unlocked, and the spirits of those trapped in Bastardhall rise up to aid the PCs. All weapon Strikes made by PCs deal an additional 1 spirit damage for the rest of the Adventure Path. Jinnivere's Riding Crop **Source** [Pathfinder #224: Bastion of Blasphemies](/Sources.aspx?ID=357) pg. 235 **Bulk** L --- When this leather riding crop is Returned, the cellars (detailed in Chapter 3) are unlocked. Companions are now more hearty and full of life—PC companions (such as familiars, eidolons, and animal companions) gain a +1 status bonus to all saving throws for the remainder of this Adventure Path. Raudltz's Telescope **Source** [Pathfinder #224: Bastion of Blasphemies](/Sources.aspx?ID=357) pg. 235 **Bulk** L --- When this handheld telescope is Returned, the fallen temple (detailed in Chapter 7) is unlocked. Secrets are now more difficult to hide in Bastardhall. Reduce all Perception DCs made when [Seeking](/Actions.aspx?ID=2301) or [Searching](/Actions.aspx?ID=2630) by 2 for the rest of this Adventure Path. Ryhasphinea's Hourglass **Source** [Pathfinder #224: Bastion of Blasphemies](/Sources.aspx?ID=357) pg. 235 **Bulk** L --- When this cracked hourglass is Returned, the vaults (detailed in Chapter 8) are unlocked. Death’s grasp on the PCs wanes—for the rest of this Adventure Path, the DCs for all recovery checks made by a [dying](/Conditions.aspx?ID=69) PC are reduced by 2.

This _[+2 greater striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2861) [maul](/Weapons.aspx?ID=388)_ is a marvel of magical and mechanical engineering, designed thousands of years ago by the mages of the Jistka Imperium for the express purpose of disabling any of the Imperium’s countless magical constructs and automatons that might turn against their creators. When you damage a construct with a Strike from the _Jistkan colossus crusher_, you deal an additional 1d6 [persistent force damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=86). This oversized [greataxe](/Weapons.aspx?ID=376), infamous for the chilling laughter it emits whenever it takes a life, was crafted by the frost giant sorcerer Jorngarl from the _final blade_ named Toothy Morris after it was stolen in an attack on a Gray Gardener convoy. </row>

---

Journeybread contains a mix of fruits, nuts, and grains with an alchemical boost. Eating one journeybread provides all the food and water you need for a day. If you subsist on nothing else for a week, you become temporarily immune to journeybread until you eat real food and drink water normally for 24 hours.

The number of minutes you can [Hustle](/Actions.aspx?ID=515) changes to your Constitution modifier × 20. These benefits last for 4 hours.

fields.text: Item 1+ Journeybread Uncommon Alchemical Consumable Source Treasure Vault pg. 49 Usage held in 1 hand Activate Single Action Interact Journeybread contains a mix of fruits, nuts, and grains with an alchemical boost. Eating one journeybread provides all the food and water you need for a day. If you subsist on nothing else for a week, you become temporarily immune to journeybread until you eat real food and drink water normally for 24 hours. Item 1 Journeybread Source Treasure Vault pg. 49 Price 3 gp Item 4 Journeybread (Power) Source Treasure Vault pg. 49 Price 15 gp In addition to the benefits of journeybread, power journeybread grants you a +1 item bonus to Athletics checks to Climb, Force Open, and Swim, and to Fortitude saving throws against being sickened. The number of minutes you can Hustle changes to your Constitution modifier × 20. These benefits last for 4 hours.

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 126 **Usage** affixed to armor or a weapon --- The golden religious symbol on the top of this spherical incense holder shifts its form to match the faith of its bearer. You gain no benefit from a judgment thurible if you don’t worship a deity. The spell DC of any spell cast by activating this item is 27.
  • **Armor** After you cast a spell by activating the thurible, the thurible casts 3rd-rank [_protection_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1641) on you, with a duration of 1 round.
  • **Weapon** After you cast a spell by activating the thurible, the weapon gains a rune that lasts until the end of your next turn. It gains the [_holy_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2842) rune if your deity allows holy sanctification or the [_unholy_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2851) rune if your deity allows unholy sanctification. If your deity allows both, you can choose which rune the weapon gains. If your deity allows neither, your weapon doesn’t gain a rune.
**Activate** Cast a Spell; **Effect** You cast [_divine lance_](/Spells.aspx?ID=84). fields.text: Item 10+ Judgement Thurible Evocation Magical Spellheart Source Treasure Vault pg. 126 Usage affixed to armor or weapon The golden religious symbol on the top of this spherical incense holder shifts its form to match the faith of its bearer. You gain no benefit from a judgment thurible if you don't worship a deity or if your deity is true neutral. The spell DC of any spell cast by activating this item is 27. Armor After you cast a spell by activating the thurible, the thurible casts circle of protection on you, with a duration of 1 round. You choose the alignment, which must be one opposed by one of your deity's alignments. Weapon After you cast a spell by activating the thurible, the weapon gains your choice of an anarchic, axiomatic, holy , or unholy rune until the end of your next turn. You can choose a rune only if it matches an alignment your deity has ( anarchic for chaotic , axiomatic for lawful, holy for good, or unholy for evil). Activate Cast a Spell; Effect You cast divine lance . Item 10 Judgment Thurible Source Treasure Vault pg. 126 Price 975 gp Activate Cast a Spell; Frequency once per day; Effect You cast divine wrath . Item 17 Judgment Thurible (Major) Source Treasure Vault pg. 126 Price 14,000 gp The additional damage from the rune granted by the thurible is 2d6, and the spell DC is 35. Activate Cast a Spell; Frequency once per day; Effect You cast 6th-level divine wrath. Activate Cast a Spell; Frequency once per day; Effect You cast divine decree . Item 20 Judgment Thurible (Greater) Source Treasure Vault pg. 126 Price 65,000 gp The additional damage from the rune granted by the thurible is 2d6, and the spell DC is 43. Activate Cast a Spell; Frequency once per day; Effect You cast 7th-level divine decree . Activate Cast a Spell; Frequency once per day; Effect You cast summon deific herald .

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 4"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Jug of Fond Remembrance](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2193)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 115

**Price** 75 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This large jug always seems to contain just enough of the holder's favorite alcohol to share with a friend. As long as you're holding the jug, you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) checks. If you share a sip of the liquor from the jug with a creature, you gain a +2 circumstance bonus to your next Diplomacy check to [Make an Impression](/Actions.aspx?ID=50) or [Request](/Actions.aspx?ID=51) something from that creature any time within the next month.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per hour;   **Effect** You take a long swig on the jug and then [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=26) about a creature you can see, with a +2 circumstance bonus to the check. If you fail but don't critically fail this check, you get a success instead. You're then [stupefied 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=37) for 3 rounds.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

**Drawback** You take a –2 penalty to Will saves, Perception checks, and initiative rolls.

After you drink this mutagen, your body becomes thick and sturdy. You exhibit a healthy glow, though you tend to be ponderous and unobservant. 

**Benefit** You gain an item bonus to Fortitude saves and the listed number of temporary Hit Points. Whenever you are at maximum Hit Points for at least 1 full minute, you regain the temporary Hit Points. 

**Drawback** You take a –2 penalty to Will saves, Perception checks, and initiative rolls.

fields.text: Item 0 Juggernaut Mutagen Alchemical Consumable Elixir Mutagen Polymorph Source Core Rulebook pg. 548 Usage held in 1 hand Bulk L Activate Single Action Interact After you drink this mutagen, your body becomes thick and sturdy. You exhibit a healthy glow, though you tend to be ponderous and unobservant. Benefit You gain an item bonus to Fortitude saves and the listed number of temporary Hit Points. Whenever you are at maximum Hit Points for at least 1 full minute, you regain the temporary Hit Points. Drawback You take a –2 penalty to Will saves, Perception checks, and initiative rolls.

<title

    pfs="Standard"
>
[Juggernaut Mutagen](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3318)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Alchemical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=528" />
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=564" />
<trait label="Elixir" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=589" />
<trait label="Mutagen" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=808" />
<trait label="Polymorph" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=670" />

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 289

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Single Action" /><row>([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104))</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

---

Your body becomes sturdy and ponderous. 

**Benefit** You gain an item bonus to Fortitude saves and the listed number of temporary Hit Points. Whenever you're at maximum Hit Points for at least 1 minute, you regain the temporary Hit Points. 

**Drawback** You take a –2 penalty to Will saves, Perception checks, and initiative rolls.

</title>

<traits>

<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Battlecry!](/Sources.aspx?ID=268) pg. 122

**Price** 35,000 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn armor

**Bulk** 4
</row>

<row gap="medium">
**Base Armor** [Full Plate](/Armor.aspx?ID=50)
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

When you are wearing this armor, you’re a veritable battering ram. This _[+3 greater resilient ](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2804) [fortification ](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2789) [full plate](/Armor.aspx?ID=50)_ is topped with a reinforced helmet shaped like a ram’s head that enables you to smash through doors and gates.

**Activate—Ram** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per hour;   **Effect** You [Stride](/Actions.aspx?ID=2305) up to 60 feet in a straight [line](/Rules.aspx?ID=2388). If you end your movement adjacent to an enemy, object, or structure, you can smash it. If you smash an enemy, you deal bludgeoning damage equal to the total distance traveled (DC 39 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2297) Fortitude save). Objects and structures you smash take damage equal to twice the distance traveled.

</title>

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

---

This well-worn manuscript is side stitched with fading lilac-colored thread. It is filled with poems written long ago by a philosopher named Seiji Juubun, which contain a lifetime of wisdom, presenting information and advice on a tremendous breadth of topics.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> envision ([emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=590), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647), [metamagic](/Traits.aspx?ID=107));  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** If your next action is to Cast a Spell that has the linguistic trait and that targets 1 creature, you are overtaken by Juubun's spirit, and the spoken elements of your spell become impactfully poetic. If the target is an ally, your words inspire them and they gain 10 temporary Hit Points, which last for 1 minute. If the targeted creature is an enemy and the spell requires a saving throw, and if the enemy fails its saving throw, they become sickened 1 as a result of despair and sadness.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Conjuration" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=33" />
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=36" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Teleportation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=156" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Grand Bazaar](/Sources.aspx?ID=100) pg. 19

**Price** 225 gp

<row gap="medium">
**Ammunition** any

</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Single Action" /><row>Interact</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

_Juxtaposition ammunition_ quivers with anticipation, as if the projectile wishes to constantly be in motion. When an activated _juxtaposition ammunition_ hits a creature, it doesn't deal the Strike's normal damage. Instead, the target must succeed at a DC 28 Will save or be teleported to a safe, unoccupied square of your choice within 60 feet of its original position and within the weapon's first range increment. On a critical failure, the target is also [sickened 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=34) from the gut-wrenching sensation of sudden movement. Any relocation from the _juxtaposition ammunition_ is [forced movement](/Rules.aspx?ID=451).

Though most aren’t made from true jyoti feathers, as the reclusive outsiders avoid visitors from the Material Plane, their connection to positive energy lent the spellhearts their name. Armor You gain a +2 item bonus to saving throws against death effects and negative energy. Weapon The weapon has the disrupting rune while the feather is affixed. Activate Cast a Spell; Effect You cast stabilize . Item 10 Jyoti's Feather Source Treasure Vault pg. 126 Price 960 gp Activate Three Actions command (emotion, enchantment, incapacitation); Requirements The target must be fascinated by the mirror; Effect You control the target for 30 days, with the effect of a critically failed saving throw against dominate . If the victim sees the mirror again at any point before this duration expires, the control extends for an additional 30 days from the moment it looked at the mirror again. While there is no initial saving throw, the DC to break free due to commands against the creature’s nature is 35. Item 14 Jyoti's Feather (Greater) Source Treasure Vault pg. 126 Price 4,100 gp The item bonus when affixed to armor is +3. Activate Cast a Spell; Frequency once per day; Effect You cast 5th-level vital beacon . Activate Cast a Spell; Frequency once per day; Effect You cast healing well . Item 16 Jyoti's Feather (Major) Source Treasure Vault pg. 126 Price 9,400 gp The item bonus when affixed to armor is +4, and the rune when affixed to a weapon is greater disrupting . Activate Cast a Spell; Frequency once per day; Effect You cast 6th-level healing well . Activate Cast a Spell; Frequency once per day; Effect You cast field of life .

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 13"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Kaiju Fulu](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2038)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=36" />
<trait label="Fulu" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=378" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 78

**Price** 500 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Duration** 1 week

**Usage** affixed to a load-bearing wall or pillar

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Despite the name, a _kaiju fulu_ protects a building against damage of all sorts. When an affixed structure no larger than 100 feet × 100 feet and up to 50 feet tall takes damage, the structure is as hard as [standard-grade adamantine](/Equipment.aspx?ID=271) against that damage and any damage that occurs within 1 hour thereafter. The fulu then crumbles to dust, and its effects end.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 20"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Kaldemash's Lament](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1890)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Unique" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=161" />
<trait label="Arcane" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=11" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 38

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Resembling little more than a simple iron pipe with a handle, _Kaldemash's Lament_ is one of the most well-known star guns in all of Arcadia. Legends state the Crowned Regent Kaldemash helped forge one of the first star guns millennia ago. While the star gun served Kaldemash as a powerful weapon, its most notable achievement was the accidental killing of one of Kaldemash's greatest friends. This death is what caused the regent to recognize the true destructive power of the star guns and led to him developing the Star Code, a set of rules of engagement and proper use of firearms still in use in Arcadia today. Although Kaldemash never named the weapon himself, all legends that mention the weapon refer to it as _Kaldemash's Lament_.

 The legendary weapon is a _+3 [major striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=280) [ quickstrike](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2844)_ advanced firearm with a range increment of 90 feet. It deals 4d6 force damage (with the _major striking_ rune included) and has the [concealable](/Traits.aspx?ID=327), [concussive](/Traits.aspx?ID=401), and [fatal d10](/Traits.aspx?ID=178) traits. You don't take a penalty when dealing nonlethal damage with the weapon. Like most star guns, _Kaldemash's Lament_ uses magic to function and doesn't require ammunition or [black powder](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1190).

 If you use _Kaldemash's Lament_ as part of a duel in which all parties are in agreement on the terms, the gun's supernatural instincts help you make the quickest draw. You roll twice and take the higher result on your initiative roll for the duel; this is a [fortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=76) effect. In addition, you can draw _Kaldemash's Lament_ as a free action at the start of your turn during the duel. If you attempt to fire the star gun in bad faith at a dueling opponent once they have surrendered, been defeated, or the duel is over, _Kaldemash's Lament_ flies out of your hand and you can't pick it up, hold it, or wield it for 10 minutes.

**Activate** <actions string="Free Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561))  **Trigger** You target a creature with an attack;  **Effect** You adjust the damage that _Kaldemash's Lament_ deals before firing. _Kaldemash's Lament's_ damage type changes to either electricity, fire, or force until you change the type again.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per minute;   **Effect** You leave _Kaldemash's Lament_ to fire on its own. You release the star gun and it begins to move independently, flying through the air and firing. You still gain the benefits of the gun's [speed](/Equipment.aspx?ID=304) rune while it's moving independently. It has a space of 5 feet but doesn't block or impede enemies attempting to move through that space. It always remains within 30 feet of you and intentionally resists being taken or otherwise moved; all attempts to [Grab](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=18) it fail. _Kaldemash's Lament_ moves this way for 3 rounds, after which it returns to your hand. If you don't have a free hand to hold it, the gun instead holsters itself on your person.

 While _Kaldemash's Lament_ is moving independently, you can command it to make a Strike against a creature as an action, which has the [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32) trait. It makes a ranged Strike using your attack modifier while wielding it or a +31 bonus, whichever is higher. This attack increases your multiple attack penalty as normal, and the gun uses your multiple attack penalty when determining its attack bonus. Since the star gun is constantly moving and attempting to line up the appropriate shot, creatures it targets are [flat-footed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=16) to the gun's attacks.

**Activate** <actions string="Three Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645))    **Effect** You unleash a barrage of attacks in an instant. You deal Strike damage to all creatures in a 30-foot cone (DC 45 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save). This barrage counts as three attacks for your multiple attack penalty.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

May contain spoilers from Sky King's Tomb **Source** [Pathfinder #194: Cult of the Cave Worm](/Sources.aspx?ID=209) pg. 78 **Bulk** 1 --- This grimoire is constructed from individual tarnished silver plates, bound together to form a fine book. Each “page” contain engraved maps, accounts of sites in Nar-Voth, and daily journals. Throughout the journal, spells and notes are inscribed on the margins and within the text. When Chapter One is completed, this grimoire contains the following spells: [_allfood_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1425), [_deep sight_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1426), [_fate's travels_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1427), [_glowing trail_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1428), [_know location_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1429), [_stonesense_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1430), [_wanderer's guide_](/Spells.aspx?ID=368). If you use the grimoire during your daily preparations and are capable of preparing spells of the appropriate level, when you cast a non-damaging spell prepared from this grimoire, you can Step or Stride up to half your Speed after Casting the Spell. To scribe additional spells into the grimoire, you must provide additional silver plates at the cost of 10 gp per spell when Learning the Spell. **Forming the Bond** The PCs locate and bind together the silver plates for Chapter One.
**Advancing the Bond** Locate additional chapters of the journal and bind them together.
**Minor Gifts** [ease burden](/Relics.aspx?ID=25), [word of faith](/Relics.aspx?ID=15)
**Major Gifts** [underground bounty](/Relics.aspx?ID=29)

Originally brought to Absalom by [kayals](/Ancestries.aspx?ID=30) fleeing the [Shadow Plane](/Planes.aspx?ID=11), kayalinis are shy creatures made from shadow. They resemble small [monkeys](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1685) with reptilian features like claws, short horns, and long, shadowy tongues. When in a new home, they tend to hide under beds or in closets. Around people they trust, they'll sit quietly on a lap for hours.

---

The edges of a _keen_ weapon are preternaturally sharp. Attacks with this weapon are a critical hit on a 19 on the die as long as that result is a success. This property has no effect on a 19 if the result would be a failure.

**Source** [Highhelm](/Sources.aspx?ID=204) pg. 113 --- The crowning achievement of Highhelm's millennia of metallurgical advancements and engineering is the beautiful alloy called keep stone. Despite its name, no stone is used in the production of keep stone. Through the use of a highly guarded process that smelts together [adamantine](/Equipment.aspx?ID=271) and lead, Highhelm's greatest crafters were able to develop a material with an appearance that more closely resembles marble than metal. Keep stone is only slightly weaker than adamantine alone, but with the incredible ability to disrupt magic. Any spell or magical effect targeting raw keep stone must succeed at a DC 5 flat check or the effect is lost. Keep stone's use in the construction of Torag's Shield is not only to stretch Highhelm's adamantine reserves further and protect the walls from magical assault, but also because of its protective effects on [divination](/Traits.aspx?ID=47) magic on both Highhelm itself and its immediate vicinity. If the target of a divination spell is in the presence of a large quantity of keep stone, including a structure, the caster must also succeed at a DC 5 flat check or the spell is lost. ## Keep Stone

>
[Keep Stone Amulet](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3767)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Shining Kingdoms](/Sources.aspx?ID=265) pg. 101

**Price** 38,000 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

The superior [adamantine](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2915)-lead alloy known as keep stone is as highly prized as it is expensive, and for good reason: keep stone combines the Hardness and durability of the finest metal with inherent magical protection. Not only does the metal itself resist magical effects, but anyone in proximity to a large amount of it also enjoys a degree of protection from divination magic. Dwarven crafters have attempted to make this extra protection more portable and more affordable in the form of _keep stone amulets_. Each amulet is unique in its exact shape, size, thickness, and decorations, but typically, a _keep stone amulet_ is roughly palm-sized and engraved with clan symbols, holy aphorisms, or a favorite line of poetry. 

While wearing a _keep stone amulet_, if you’re the target of a spell with the [detection](/Traits.aspx?ID=574) or [scrying](/Traits.aspx?ID=689) trait, the caster must succeed at a DC 5 [flat check](/Rules.aspx?ID=333) or lose the spell.

**Activate—Rebuff Magic** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [misfortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=654)) **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** You’re the target of a spell with a [spell attack roll](/Rules.aspx?ID=2292);  **Effect** The caster must roll the spell attack roll twice and take the worse result.
