Life shot is a special cartridge that carries a small dose of [elixir of life](/Equipment.aspx?ID=91). A creature hit by activated life shot takes no damage from the successful attack, instead receiving healing and gaining an item bonus to saving throws against [diseases](/Traits.aspx?ID=46) and [poisons](/Traits.aspx?ID=126) for 1 minute. On a critical hit, roll the healing received twice and take the better result (this is a [fortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=76) effect). A target willing to be hit by this attack is [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) against it.

</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Extinction Curse</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Unique" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=161" />
<trait label="Evil" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=64" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Necromancy" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=117" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #155: Lord of the Black Sands](/Sources.aspx?ID=33) pg. 76

**Price** 23,500 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** 2
</row>

<row gap="medium">
**Base Weapon** [Rhoka Sword](/Weapons.aspx?ID=120)
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

The twin serrated blades of this legendary [rhoka sword](/Weapons.aspx?ID=120) are dull black and constantly drip with blood. _Life's Last Breath_ is said to have been forged centuries ago for an unknown [urdefhan](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=158) general and has since fallen into the hands of countless other powerful urdefhan warlords.

 _Life's Last Breath_ is a _+3 greater striking [unholy](/Equipment.aspx?ID=307) [wounding](/Equipment.aspx?ID=309) rhoka sword_ with the following special abilities.

**Activate** <actions string="Reaction" /> command;  **Frequency** once per day;  **Requirements** You successfully Strike a creature with _Life's Last Breath_; **Effect** You cast a 9th-level [_paralyze_](/Spells.aspx?ID=213) spell on the target.

**Activate** <actions string="Reaction" /> envision;  **Frequency** once per 10 minutes; **Trigger** You successfully Strike a creature with _Life's Last Breath_;  **Effect** The target must succeed at a DC 38 Fortitude save or take 4d6 negative damage; you gain an equal amount of temporary Hit Points that last 1 minute.

While wearing the armor, you feel at ease knowing the armor can protect you in even dire circumstances. The gemstone glows with life essence, casting green light as brightly as a torch. You can suppress or resume this light by using a single action, which has the [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32) trait.
**Activate—Second Chance** ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32)) **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** You would die; **Effect** The armor’s gemstone turns gray as it shares life energy with you. The armor casts [_breath of life_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1456) on you. **Activate—Shielding Light** ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104)) **Effect** You tap on the gemstone, producing a protective screen of green light. You cast a 5th-rank [_shield_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1671) spell. As normal with the spell, you can’t cast shield again (using this activation or other means) for 10 minutes if you use it to [Shield Block](/Feats.aspx?ID=5212). While wearing the armor, you feel at ease knowing the armor can protect you in even dire circumstances. The gemstone glows with life essence, casting green light as brightly as a torch. You can suppress or resume this light by using a single action, which has the concentrate trait. You cast a 5th-rank shield spell. As normal with the spell, you can’t cast shield again (using this activation or other means) for 10 minutes if you use it to Shield Block. </title>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Bulk** L
</row>

---

This wide leather belt grants you a +1 item bonus to Athletics checks and increases the amount you can easily carry. You can carry Bulk equal to 6 + your Strength modifier before becoming encumbered, and you can hold and carry a total Bulk up to 11 + your Strength modifier. 

**Activate—Assisted Lift** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104))    **Effect** You lift an object of up to 8 Bulk as though it were weightless. This requires two hands, and if the object is locked or otherwise held in place, you can attempt to Force it Open using Athletics as part of this activation. The object still has its full weight and Bulk for all other purposes—you just ignore that weight. The effect lasts until the end of your next turn.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 6"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Light Writer](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1152)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Clockwork" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=331" />
<trait label="Light" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=100" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 88

_[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) All Pathfinder Society agents have access to all uncommon clockwork items and gadgets from Chapters 1 and 2 of this book_

**Price** 200 gp (3 gp for 10 metal plates)

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk** 2
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

The light writer is a cutting edge invention, first created in Absalom in late 4721, combining magic and clockwork innovation to allow its operator to create a true-to-life, monochromatic portrait of people or a scene over the course of 20 minutes of exposure. It consists of two flat metal squares, one larger than the other, connected by a tube of leather similar to that found on a bellows. The smaller square, which sits at the front of the device, has a small glass lens in the center of it. The larger square contains a specially treated metallic plate on the inside; its exterior also has both a small control stick connected via flexible wire, and a small metal tube attached to the top and pointing forward. The user presses a button on the control stick to activate the light writer. Upon activation, magical light illuminates the tube, producing a steady light for 20 minutes. This light is captured by the lens and projected onto the metal plate, slowly creating an image of the scene in front of the lens. The plate can then be removed, allowing the image to be displayed anywhere the owner desires. The light writer is mounted on a tripod and must be perfectly still during operation to prevent any defects from appearing in the plate image. The smaller square, which sits at the front of the device, has a small glass lens in the center of it. The user presses a button on the control stick to activate the _light writer_. Upon activation, magical light illuminates the tube, producing a steady light for 20 minutes. This light is captured by the lens and projected onto the metal plate, slowly creating an image of the scene in front of the lens. The plate can then be removed, allowing the image to be displayed anywhere the owner desires. The _light writer_ is mounted on a tripod and must be perfectly still during operation to prevent any defects from appearing in the plate image. If creating a captured image of a living creature, it is equally important for that creature to remain still throughout the process, to avoid a ghostlike blurring of the final image.

>
[Lightning Rod Shot](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2053)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=36" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 82

**Price** 60 gp

<row gap="medium">
**Ammunition** any

</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Single Action" /><row>([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561))</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Made from a shaft of silver with a gleaming copper tip, the _lightning rod shot_ crackles with electricity as it flies through the air. When a _lightning rod shot_ strikes a target, it remains intact. It moves with a creature it struck, unless the GM determines otherwise, until that creature regains any Hit Points. If it doesn't stick to the target, it falls to the ground and becomes inactive. If the target of this shot is within 10 feet of any creature or target that takes electricity damage, the target of this shot takes 1 electricity damage for each die of damage taken by the nearby creature or target. If the target of this shot takes electricity damage from a spell or attack, it also takes 1 additional electricity damage for each die of damage dealt. If the spell or attack allows a saving throw to reduce the damage, the target of this shot takes a –1 circumstance penalty to the save. This shot remains active for 1 minute, after which it falls to the ground and crumbles to dust.

</column>

fields.markdown:
**Source** [Cheliax, Infernal Inheritence](/Sources.aspx?ID=372) pg. 103 **Price** 215 gp **Usage** held in 1 hand **Bulk** L --- Popular among smugglers and other sailors of ill repute, this unassuming palm-sized wooden lily pad or lotus leaf expands on command, forming a floating platform. **Activate—Expand** ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day; **Effect** You place the _lily pad platform_ on the surface of a body of water at least 60 feet deep. It instantly unfolds into a flat platform that fills a 20-foot burst or the entire body of water, whichever is smaller. Any creatures or items in the area are lifted on top of it, and it’s anchored in place, unmoved by the current.

You can use a single action with the [auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=541) trait to instantly return the _lily pad platform_ to its original size, dropping any items or creatures on it into the water. This happens automatically if the total Bulk of items and creatures on the _lily pad platform_ exceeds 100 Bulk. **Activate—Plunge** ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=541)) **Requirements** The _lily pad platform_ is expanded; **Effect** The _lily pad platform_ wraps around everything on top of it and plunges 60 feet beneath the surface for 1 hour, after which it returns to the surface. While submerged, items take no damage from the water, and creatures can breathe normally but are engulfed ([Escape](/Actions.aspx?ID=2296) DC 19).

This [tower shield](/Shields.aspx?ID=4) is a slab of limestone, shaved to a portable size and weight. The shield has Hardness 7 and 28 Hit Points.

**Activate—Limestone Wall** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You set the shield down as it expands up to 60 feet wide and 10 feet tall. Each square of the wall has AC 10, Hardness 7, and 28 Hit Points, and it's immune to critical hits and precision damage. If a section is destroyed, this effect ends, and your limestone shield is broken. You can Dismiss this activation, which otherwise lasts for 1 minute.

    level="1"
    right="Item 24"
    pfs="Restricted"
>
[Limitless Power](/Equipment.aspx?ID=5234)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=683" />
<trait label="Artifact" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=537" />
<trait label="Contract" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=329" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=637" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=644" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Cheliax, Infernal Inheritence](/Sources.aspx?ID=372) pg. 80

_[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) Pathfinder Society agents should not strike deals with devils without Decemvirate approval._

<row gap="medium">

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Each of these _bargained contracts_ is unique, matching the contracted's idea of unlimited power. When you gain this contract, select one weapon in your possession, a common [divine cantrip](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=2), and one common divine spell of each spell rank except 10th. The weapon becomes a _[+4 greater striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2861)_ weapon. Once per day, from any distance, when you Activate this contract or Strike with the selected weapon, the devil who holds your _bargained contract_ can call upon their divine right as a free action to have the spell or Strike target you or have its area centered on you instead of its intended targets. 

**Activate—Unholy Demand** <actions string="Three Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per week;   **Effect** You call upon a right of self-determination article in your contract. The contract casts _[manifestation](/Spells.aspx?ID=1592)_ (spell attack modifier +30, DC 40). Your contractor is immediately made aware of which spell you are duplicating. 

**Activate—Unleash Power** <actions string="Single Action to Three Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645))    **Effect** The contract casts one of the selected spells (spell attack modifier +30, DC 40). The contract can cast each non-cantrip spell only once per day. You use the same number of actions for this activation as the selected spell normally takes.

**Destruction** The contract bursts into flame if the devil who signed it is slain and a celestial of equal or higher level declares it void.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

---

This luminescent white gem glows from within, and a weapon it’s applied to gains its inner radiance, shedding dim light in a 10-foot radius. Successful Strikes with a weapon affected by a _limning gem_ outline the target in a [bright white light](/Rules.aspx?ID=2402); if the target was [invisible](/Conditions.aspx?ID=83), it becomes [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=62) instead. This light lasts until the end of your next turn or for the remainder of the limning gem’s duration on a critical hit.

>
[Linnorm's Sankeit](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1849)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 18

**Price** 22,750 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn armor

**Bulk** 2
</row>

<row gap="medium">
**Base Armor** [Sankeit](/Armor.aspx?ID=34)
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

The first suit of _+3 [greater resilient](/Equipment.aspx?ID=279) [antimagic](/Equipment.aspx?ID=282) [sankeit](/Armor.aspx?ID=34)_ made in this fashion was crafted for the Varki linnorm king Nankou, after he claimed his title by slaying a [taiga linnorm](/Monsters.aspx?ID=723). By Varki tradition, the armor was crafted using some of the slain linnorm's body to decorate the breastplate and helm, which imbued the armor with several of the linnorm's natural abilities. Though the helm is shaped like the beast's head, a linnorm's actual head would be too large for a proper helmet.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per hour;   **Effect** You breathe a 60-foot cone of electrified vapor, dealing 17d6 electricity damage to creatures in the area (DC 38 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save). The electrified mist persists in the area for 2 rounds, dealing 5d6 electricity damage (DC 38 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save) to each creature that ends its turn in the mist. If you slew the linnorm this armor is made from, you can use the higher of your class DC or spell DC instead of the listed DCs for this effect.

**Activate** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645))  **Trigger** A creature adjacent to you targets you with a melee attack;  **Effect** The creature takes 4d6 piercing damage as previously invisible magical spines leap outwards from the armor to punish them for the attack.

**Craft Requirements** The initial raw materials must include the hide and skull of any type of [linnorm](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=439).

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 12+"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Lion's Armor](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2807)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=637" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=644" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [GM Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=218) pg. 230

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn armor

**Bulk** 3
</row>

<row gap="medium">
**Base Armor** [Half Plate](/Armor.aspx?ID=49)
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Various parts of this _+2 [resilient](/Equipment.aspx?ID=279) [half plate](/Armor.aspx?ID=49)_ are forged into the shape of a lion’s head. The golden lion heads grant you a commanding presence and seem to actively growl at your enemies, granting you a +2 item bonus to [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7).

The lions on the armor work in tandem with the lion on a _[lion's shield](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2823)_. If you critically hit with the _lion’s shield_ using Lion Bite, the lions on the armor roar in support of the shield, causing the target of the shield’s Strike to become [frightened 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=19). 

**Activate—Roar of the Pride** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** The lions on your armor roar, attempting to cow your enemies. Attempt a check to [Demoralize](/Actions.aspx?ID=53) each enemy within 30 feet of you. On a critical success, the target is also [fleeing](/Conditions.aspx?ID=17) for 1 round.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 10"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Lion's Call](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3777)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Shining Kingdoms](/Sources.aspx?ID=265) pg. 173

**Price** 900 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

**Access** You’re a member of the Lion Blades.

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Given only to highly trusted agents by the grand princes back when Lion Blades protected the Primogen Crown, these historic _[+1 striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2861) [ authorized](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1864) [ shortswords](/Weapons.aspx?ID=398)_ allow a Lion Blade wielder to locate resources. 

**Activate—Find the Pride** <actions string="Three Actions" /> ([arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=534), [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You cast [_locate_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1588) at 5th rank to learn the location of one of the following of your choice: the nearest Lion Blade safe house, shadow school, Lion Blade agent, Lion Blade kith, or a person other than yourself who’s in possession of a _lion’s call_.

**Activate—Echo the Call** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=534), [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** A creature locates you using another _lion’s call_;  **Effect** You immediately learn the location and appearance of the triggering creature. You can communicate [telepathically](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=79) with the triggering creature while you remain within 1 mile of each other for the next hour.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

</row>

**Access** You’re a member of the Lion Blades.

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Laurisa Tromaine ordered these as prototype uniforms. The fur-lined pauldrons bear the insignia of a lion with a blade in its mouth. The type of blade indicates which bard school one graduated from. When you disguise the armor via its [_raiment_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2791) rune, you can choose whether to conceal this symbol or not. You can also use the rune’s activation to quickly display or hide the insignia.

**Activate—Contact Ally** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=534), [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per hour;   **Effect** You cast [_message_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1598) at 1st rank to a target that you know is also wearing a _lion’s pelt_ uniform. If you and the target share an insignia, the spell is heightened to 3rd rank.

    right="Item 6"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Lion's Shield](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2823)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=644" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [GM Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=218) pg. 234

**Price** 245 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** 1
</row>

<row gap="medium">
**Base Shield** [Steel Shield](/Shields.aspx?ID=19)
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This steel shield (Hardness 6, HP 36, BT 18) is forged into the shape of a roaring lion's head. The lion's head functions as _+1 striking_ [shield boss](/Weapons.aspx?ID=41) that can't be removed from the shield. 

**Activate—Lion's Bite** <actions string="Free Action" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104)) **Frequency** once per day;  **Requirements** Your Shield is raised; **Effect** You animate the lion's head, making a melee Strike with it. The shield's biting maw is a martial melee weapon that deals 2d6 piercing damage and has the [deadly](/Traits.aspx?ID=174) d6 trait; it can't be enhanced by runes. The shield remains animated for 1 minute, during which time you can Strike with it each time you [Raise the Shield](/Actions.aspx?ID=98), as well as with a Strike action.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 215 **Price** 30 gp **Usage** held in 1 hand **Bulk** L **Activate**Cast a Spell --- This carved effigy of a lemur clutches a pen and paper, its expression cackling gleefully. When used as a catalyst to cast a _[_mad monkeys_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1590)_ spell, the following option is added to the options normally available.
**• Fierce Debate** The monkeys appear frantically scribbling on conjured paper before turning on each other in a fit of rage; those who can speak with animals understand the dispute to be broadly over prose, spelling, and grammar. Creatures in the spell’s area are met with a flurry of paper and fur as the resulting fracas obstructs their sight. When the spell ends, paper and pens conjured by this spell disappear. **Critical Success** The creature is unaffected and is temporarily immune for 10 minutes.
**Success** The creature is unaffected.
**Failure** The creature is [dazzled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=65) for 1 round.
**Critical Failure** The creature is [blinded](/Conditions.aspx?ID=59) for 1 round.

The _Liver Bloodstone of Arazni_ represents confidence. While holding the _Liver Bloodstone_, you feel more certain in your abilities.

**Activate—Embolden** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per hour; **Trigger** You critically succeed on an attack roll, saving throw, or skill check while in [encounter mode](/Rules.aspx?ID=2421);  **Effect** You gain [temporary Hit Points](/Rules.aspx?ID=2321) equal to your level for 1 round.

**Activate—Arazni's Fervor** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day;  **Requirements** You worship [Arazni](/Deities.aspx?ID=326) or are favored by her; **Effect** You hold the _Liver Bloodstone_ aloft, and the _Bloodstone_ glows with crimson light, filling you and your allies with Arazni’s wrath. The Liver Bloodstone casts [_bless_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1451). For the next minute, you can use a free action at the beginning of each of your turns to increase the spell’s [emanation](/Rules.aspx?ID=2387) radius by 10 feet. You can’t increase the emanation’s radius in any other way.

**Destruction** The _Liver Bloodstone_ melts into a puddle of poison if a worshipper of Arazni willingly submerges the _Bloodstone_ in a lethal contact or consumed [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=669), then licks the _Bloodstone_ clean. Each creature in a 15-foot [emanation](/Rules.aspx?ID=2387) is exposed to the poison that destroyed the _Bloodstone_, as if they’d touched or consumed that poison.

Destruction The Liver Bloodstone melts into a puddle of poison if a worshipper of Arazni willingly submerges the Bloodstone in a lethal contact or consumed poison, then licks the Bloodstone clean. Each creature in a 15-foot emanation is exposed to the poison that destroyed the Bloodstone , as if they’d touched or consumed that poison.

This suit of [leaf weave](/Armor.aspx?ID=28) armor is specially modified to metabolize the alchemical accelerants in medicinal compounds. A special receptacle in the armor can hold an [elixir of life](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3308), which takes 3 Interact actions to install.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645))   **Requirements** An elixir of life is installed in the armor; **Effect** Slithering vines grow from the armor, granting an item bonus to [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) checks to [Grapple](/Actions.aspx?ID=2376), to your Fortitude DC to resist Grapple, [Disarm](/Actions.aspx?ID=2383), or [Shove](/Actions.aspx?ID=2380) attempts, and to your Reflex DC to resist Trip attempts. Item 0 Lizard Source Travel Guide pg. 101 Price 1 sp Item 0 Lizard (X's) Source Travel Guide pg. 101 Price 1 gp Named after the druid that popularized them, these black-and-white lizards have substantial stomachs and a rather slow digestive system. X trained these lizards to keep valuables in their stomachs. They swallow specially treated purses with attached chains that clip to a collar, which can hold objects up to 1 Bulk. The contents of the purse stay safe for one month before slowly dissolving.

---

A nigh-infinite assortment of games exist in Golarion. Simple games, including dice, a deck of cards, or dominoes, cost 5 sp. Board games vary in cost from 1 gp for dexterity games like Bungle, 3 gp for colorful children's games like Cauldron Quest, and 5 gp for complex strategy games like Kingmaker and Abendego Raiders. Lavish game sets can cost much more than these prices, as they are made of expensive components and are intricately crafted works of art unto themselves.

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk** L

---

These dice are weighted on one side to ensure they always land with the desired number facing up. Loaded dice grant you a +1 item bonus to [Games Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) checks to gamble with the dice. You can determine a die is loaded while handling it with a successful secret DC 20 Perception check. Determining dice are loaded without handling the dice is more difficult, especially since smart cheaters switch loaded dice in and out so they don't suspiciously roll the same number over and over. In this case, an observer must succeed at a secret Perception check against the roller's Games Lore or [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=17) DC to notice the switches or the patterns.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 11"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Locket of Love Left Behind](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3970)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Battlecry!](/Sources.aspx?ID=268) pg. 150

_[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) Replacing the casing of a _locket of love left behind_ takes 30 days of Downtime._

**Price** 1,200 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

There’s a tiny picture of a beloved partner, child, or even place nestled inside this small gold locket with a heart on the front. The locket reminds you that no matter how terrible the ravages of war are, you have something very important to live for. While wearing the necklace, you gain a +5-foot status bonus to your Speeds when you have the [fleeing](/Conditions.aspx?ID=74) condition. If you are dying, the DC of [recovery checks](/Rules.aspx?ID=2326) is reduced by 1.

**Activate—True Love’s Power** <actions string="Reaction" /> ;   **Trigger** You would die due to a [death effect](/Rules.aspx?ID=2331) rather than the [dying](/Conditions.aspx?ID=69) condition;  **Effect** Your love pulls you back from the brink of death and the locket cracks. You avoid dying and remain at 1 Hit Point. You cannot use the ability again until you replace the casing of the locket, which typically takes around 1 month and costs 600 gp.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 19"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[Locket of Sealed Nightmares](/Equipment.aspx?ID=664)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Extinction Curse</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Illusion" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=92" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #156: The Apocalypse Prophet](/Sources.aspx?ID=36) pg. 74

**Price** 36,000 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn necklace

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

As long as this locket of horn and silver is closed, you don't need to sleep. However, you can still overexert your body with too much activity, so you still need to rest to avoid becoming [fatigued](/Conditions.aspx?ID=15) or to remove the fatigued condition. You also gain a +4 item bonus on saving throws against mental illusions, magical effects that would make you [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=38), and effects that would make you fatigued. Each time dawn occurs, you regain the ability to make your daily preparations as if you had rested for 8 hours. Daily preparations still take about an hour, as normal.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> envision, Interact;    **Requirements** You aren't fatigued; **Effect** You open the locket to unleash the dreams it has kept at bay. You become fatigued and cast one of the following spells at 9th level (DC 41): [_hallucination_](/Spells.aspx?ID=144), [_sleep_](/Spells.aspx?ID=288), or [_weird_](/Spells.aspx?ID=375).

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

</title>

<traits>

<column gap="tiny">

---

This _[+1 ](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2804) [studded leather armor](/Armor.aspx?ID=42)_ was specially designed for removing locusts and similar vermin that had swarmed over portions of the battlefield. It’s fully sealed along all of its seams with extra stitching and care, granting a +1 item bonus to Reflex saving throws against Swarming Bites, Swarming Stings, and similar abilities from swarms. In addition, you can create a cloud of smoke that can drive swarms from the area.

**Activate—Poison Fumes** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You emit a quickly fading toxic cloud around you in a 5-foot [emanation](/Rules.aspx?ID=2387). All creatures within the emanation take 5d6 poison damage (DC 24 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2297) Fortitude save). Swarms that fail this save also take 1d6 [persistent poison damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=86).

fields.text: Item 12+ Lodestone Bomb Alchemical Bomb Consumable Force Splash Source Treasure Vault pg. 44 Usage held in 1 hand Bulk L Activate Single Action Strike Lodestone bombs hold reactive ionized minerals preserved in a dormant state until broken. The bomb grants an item bonus to attack rolls and deals force damage and force splash damage, according to the bomb’s type. In addition, a target made of metal, wearing metal armor, or using metal weapons takes persistent force damage and is clumsy 1 and enfeebled 1 while taking the persistent damage. The persistent damage can last up to 1 minute. Item 12 Lodestone Bomb Source Treasure Vault pg. 44 Price 400 gp You gain a +2 item bonus to attack rolls, and the bomb deals 3d4 force damage plus 2 force splash damage. The bomb deals 2d4 persistent force damage to applicable targets. Item 18 Lodestone Bomb (Greater) Source Treasure Vault pg. 44 Price 4,500 gp You gain a +3 item bonus to attack rolls, and the bomb deals 4d4 force damage plus 3 force splash damage. The bomb deals 3d4 persistent force damage to applicable targets.

[Longnight Tea](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3142)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Season of Ghosts</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=36" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Necromancy" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=117" />
<trait label="Potion" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=130" />
<trait label="Tea" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=738" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #197: Let the Leaves Fall](/Sources.aspx?ID=222) pg. 77

**Price** 12 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Single Action" /><row>Interact or 10 minutes (concentrate, Interact)</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This tea is brewed with a mixture of matcha, turmeric, and 10 drops of morning dew, creating a fragrant but mildly bitter tea. The bitter aftertaste is said to be the most important element of _longnight tea_, for it's believed that this flavor lingers on the tongue and aids in keeping you awake and alert. The tea is favored by scholars and soldiers alike, although the value to which each attributes the ability to endure long nights without sleeping varies—and is often the subject of unusually impassioned debate. When you drink _longnight tea_, it grants you a +1 item bonus to saving throws against [sleep](/Traits.aspx?ID=696) effects for 1 hour. 

---

 [Tea Ceremony](/Traits.aspx?ID=738) The duration increases to 8 hours, and the tea removes the [fatigued](/Conditions.aspx?ID=73) condition.

</column>

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=36" />
<trait label="Illusion" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=92" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Talisman" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=155" />
<trait label="Visual" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=163" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 224

**Price** 150 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** affixed to a weapon

</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Single Action" /><row>([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561))</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This talisman takes the form of a flower from the sweetbriar rose, also called the eglantine rose, tied to the weapon with a bit of string. The talisman’s enchantment is such that the flower never wilts. When you activate it, your weapon becomes difficult to look at for 1 minute, as through a shimmer of heat or something seen out of the corner of your eye. While this effect is active, you gain a +2 status bonus to [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) checks to [Feint](/Actions.aspx?ID=2390). If you’re untrained in Deception, you can use the [Feint](/Actions.aspx?ID=1434) action anyway and add your level as your proficiency bonus despite being untrained. Additionally, your Strikes and damage from the affixed weapon can’t trigger reactions (such as the [Shield Block](/Feats.aspx?ID=5212) reaction).

---

This brass and wood [spyglass](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2754) is typically decorated with etchings of distant landscapes seen on the horizon of a vast body of water. When the spyglass is extended for use, the etchings of distant-appearing horizons appear to grow closer. A _lookout's spyglass_ can be used as a typical spyglass to see eight times farther than normal, but it also has the following activation.

**Activate—Seek Significance** <actions string="" /> 1 minute ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You spend a minute observing your surroundings in all directions through the _lookout's spyglass_, taking in the features of the terrain while the spyglass sharpens your senses of observation. Once you complete the activation, the next time within the next hour that you roll Perception for initiative, you gain a +1 item bonus on the roll if you're still carrying the _lookout's spyglass_ on your person.

The poison known as looter's lethargy ensures no thieves are strong enough to walk off with pilfered treasures. Commonly smeared on locks, chests, and even valuable items themselves, the poison slowly saps the strength of those who touch it. Nearby guardians can then simply follow the resulting trail of discarded valuables to find the weakened trespasser.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Contract" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=329" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 165

<row gap="medium">

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Sealed with a vial containing the ashes from your childhood home, you traded the memories of your early life to stay focused on the present, allowing you to avoid distractions during combat. Once per day, from any distance, the entity that holds your _bargained contract_ can take one of your memories. This functions as a casting of [_modify memory_](/Spells.aspx?ID=200) that doesn't grant you a saving throw and can't be reversed by any means without stealing the memory back first.

**Activate** <actions string="Free Action" /> command;  **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** You start your turn [flat-footed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=16) or [confused](/Conditions.aspx?ID=5);  **Effect** A speck of ash from the vial sealing your _bargained contract_ appears out of nowhere on your tongue, bringing your senses into focus. You suppress the flat-footed or confused condition until the start of your next turn. You can use this free action when you are confused, even though you normally can't take actions of your choice when confused.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

---

Sealed with a vial containing the ashes from your childhood home, you traded the memories of your early life to stay focused on the present, allowing you to avoid distractions during combat. Once per day, from any distance, the entity that holds your _bargained contract_ can take one of your memories. This functions as a casting of [_rewrite memory_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1655) that doesn't grant you a saving throw and can't be reversed by any means without stealing the memory back first. 

**Activate—Fix Focus** <actions string="Free Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** You start your turn [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) or [confused](/Conditions.aspx?ID=63);  **Effect**  A speck of ash from the vial sealing your _bargained contract_ appears out of nowhere on your tongue, bringing your senses into focus. You suppress the off-guard or confused condition until the start of your next turn. You can use this free action when you're confused, even though you normally can't take actions of your choice when confused.

</column>

---

These white silk gloves are adorned in red hearts that glow faintly whenever you are adjacent to someone you feel particularly strongly toward. They buoy your spirit, giving you a +1 item bonus to Diplomacy checks. 

**Activate—Bond** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You grasp the hands of a willing creature you have strong positive feelings about, regardless of the nature of those feelings. The creature gains a +1 status bonus to saving throws and 10 temporary Hit Points for 10 minutes. If the creature shares your feelings, you gain the same benefits, and for the duration, when you both roll a success on a saving throw against an emotion effect that causes negative emotions, you both get a critical success instead.

---

This lock of hair is wrapped around a twig twisted into the shape of a heart. Popular among many of Restov's explorers, traders, and mercenaries, often a person carries several _lover's knots_ on their person in case of emergency. While the original _lover's knots_ were specific rewards granted by a particularly flirtatious Swordlord to her favored agents, time has seen these talismans become much more widespread through southern Brevoy. When you activate a _lover's knot_, you regain 2d6 Hit Points. If you have the [Battle Medicine](/Feats.aspx?ID=760) feat, you instead regain 2d6+7 Hit Points.

[Lovers' Ink](/Equipment.aspx?ID=765)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Alchemical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=6" />
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=36" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Legends](/Sources.aspx?ID=40) pg. 24

**Price** 5 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** with writing set

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This ink, derived from inks used by lovers to deliver secret messages, dries to a color similar to most parchments. Avarneus's version requires another dose of lover's ink and a specific agitation to reveal the hidden message, preventing casual interception. Any message written with lovers' ink is revealed by applying a page worth of lover's ink and vigorously shaking, requiring 3 Interact actions. A typical vial provides enough ink to fill 1 page worth of text. While the text is hidden, a creature closely examining a surface marked with lover's ink can detect the presence of the ink with a successful DC 25 Perception check. On a critical success, they can make out the ink well enough to use [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=14) to [Decipher Writing](/Actions.aspx?ID=22).

</column>

May contain spoilers from Dead God's Hand **Source** [The Dead God's Hand](/Sources.aspx?ID=370) pg. 142 --- Throneglass is an incredibly rare resource created during the violence of Earthfall 10,000 years ago, when the impact of falling stars enhanced certain shattered panes of green glass built into the architecture of important buildings in Azlant— particularly the Imperial Palace. As a material, throneglass is as strong as steel, but the ancient methods of crafting it into weapons have long been lost. Low-grade throneglass offers no additional benefit to a weapon crafted from it other than the cosmetic and intrinsic value of the precious material, but standard-grade and high-grade throneglass can retain psychic power and then release it through a strike. When a creature wielding a standard-grade or high-grade throneglass weapon succeeds at a saving throw against a [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647) effect, the weapon stores some of that energy and holds it for a future attack. A standard-grade weapon can hold this energy for 1 round before it dissipates harmlessly, while a high-grade one can hold the energy for 1 minute. The next time you [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) a creature with a throneglass weapon with stored energy, the creature struck must attempt a Will save (DC 24 for standardgrade throneglass, or DC 35 for high-grade throneglass) to avoid becoming [stupefied](/Conditions.aspx?ID=94) 1 for 1 round (or stupefied 2 on a critical failure). ## Throneglass Items

Luck and good fortune bless the wielder of this _+3 greater striking [shortsword](/Weapons.aspx?ID=43)_. _Luck blades_ are crafted in a variety of styles, but their hilts or blades always incorporate symbols of luck, such as clovers, horseshoes, fish, ladybugs, or other symbols.

Luck blades are crafted in a variety of styles, but their hilts or blades always incorporate symbols of luck, such as clovers, horseshoes, fish, ladybugs, or other symbols. Activate Reaction envision; Frequency once per day; Trigger You miss on a Strike with the luck blade; Effect Reroll the triggering attack roll and use the new result. This is a fortune effect. Craft Requirements Supply a casting of wish Item 17 Luck Blade Source Core Rulebook pg. 601 Price 15,000 gp Item 19 Luck Blade (Wishing) Source Core Rulebook pg. 601 Price 30,000 gp Some luck blades contain one wish when crafted. >
[Luckless Dice](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2383)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=683" />
<trait label="Cursed" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=274" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Misfortune" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=110" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 192

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Carved of bone, _luckless dice_ appear to be a set of [loaded dice](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1333). If unsuccessfully identified as cursed, _luckless dice_ seem to hold a minor enchantment that improves your luck. However, they fuse to you when you use them, cursing you with ill fortune. _Luckless dice_ don't grant a bonus on [Games Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) checks. Instead, when you use them to gamble, the GM rolls secretly, granting you the lower result. Once you realize the dice are cursed, the GM can instead allow you to roll twice and take the lower result.

</column>

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 2+"
    pfs=""
>
[Lucky Coin](/Equipment.aspx?ID=4945)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Troubles in Grayce</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />
<trait label="Fortune" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=612" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=644" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Troubles in Grayce](/Sources.aspx?ID=327) pg. 118

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

These coins—copper, silver, or gold depending on their potency—were not minted for circulation. Rather, friendly fey helped to create them as wards against the abilities of some [gremlins](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=424), namely [pugwampis](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3032). The coins are said to protect the bearer against misfortunes of all stripes, though, not merely those of gremlins and have come to be seen as good luck charms the world over. Each coin, regardless of the metal used to mint it, has a canine face on both sides; on one side, the face's mouth is open in a wide smile, while the other shows the face snarling.

**Activate—Guarded Fortune** <actions string="Free Action" /> [fortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=612), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)  **Trigger** You fail a skill check due to a [misfortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=654) effect;  **Effect** Flip the coin. If it lands on the smiling face, reroll the triggering check; since this activation has the [fortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=612) effect, any misfortune effect is canceled out for this check. You must use the new result, even if it's worse. If it lands on the snarling face, nothing happens. Either way, you're temporarily immune to Guarded Fortune for 1 hour.

**Craft Requirements** Any checks made to craft this item while under a misfortune effect are automatic critical failures.

</column>

fields.markdown:
**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 180 _[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) Characters with access to firearms gain access to accessories that can be used with those weapons._ **Usage** worn **Bulk** L --- This beige bandolier has a rectangular holster, which allows it to contain a standard-sized [Harrow deck](/Equipment.aspx?ID=824), and red pockets embroidered with goldwork in a strange but appealing mixture of Alkenstar and Varisian motifs. **Activate** ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day; **Effect** You draw a card from the bandolier and Interact to load the card into a gun or crossbow you're wielding that requires 1 action to reload. The drawn card immediately transforms into magical ammunition with a type depending on the drawn card's suit, and a new copy of that card returns to the deck, ready to be drawn again. When the card transforms into ammunition, it transforms into a firearm round or crossbow bolt appropriate for the weapon you chose to reload, even if magical ammunition of the drawn variety would normally be limited to ammunition of a different type (such as a storm arrow normally only being available in arrow form). Either draw a card from the Harrow deck or roll 1d6 to determine the suit of the card. The result determines the type of magical ammunition the card becomes, as per the table below. Magical ammunition created this way lasts 10 minutes or until you fire it, whichever comes first. ## Lucky Draw Bandolier
**d6****Ability (Suit)****Ammunition**
1Strength (Hammer)[_Meteor shot_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1196)
2Dexterity (Key)[_Storm arrow_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=169)
3Constitution (Shield)[_Corrosive ammunition_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=711)
4Intelligence (Book)[_Explosive ammunition_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=162)
5Wisdom (Star)[_Terrifying ammunition](/Equipment.aspx?ID=725)
6Charisma (Crown)[_Fairy bullet_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1194)
 Lucky Draw Bandolier **Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 180 **Price** 700 gp **Bulk** L Lucky Draw Bandolier (Greater) **Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 180 **Price** 2,000 gp **Bulk** L --- You can activate a _greater lucky draw bandolier_ once per hour instead of being able to activate it once per day.

</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Blood Lords</spoilers>

---

This small doll in the shape of a witch is made from sticks and clad in a simple dress, bonnet, and wooden shoes. It sits astride a miniature straw broom. When hung in a kitchen, the witch brings good luck and protects a cook from malicious spirits. The _lucky kitchen witch_ must hang in a kitchen for a week to give any benefit.

 When you have a _lucky kitchen witch_ hung in your kitchen, you can reroll a [Cooking Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) or [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=4) check made during downtime to make food, [Earn Income](/Actions.aspx?ID=23), or [Craft](/Actions.aspx?ID=43) an [alchemical](/Traits.aspx?ID=6) item in your kitchen.

    right="Item 11"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[Lumber Lord's Axe](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3164)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Season of Ghosts</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=644" />
<trait label="Transmutation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=157" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #199: To Bloom Below the Web](/Sources.aspx?ID=225) pg. 75

**Price** 900 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** 1
</row>

<row gap="medium">
**Base Weapon** [Battle Axe](/Weapons.aspx?ID=16)
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This unassuming tool wouldn't look out of place on the belt of an industrious laborer. Grooves worn into the wooden handle over years of use and an irregularly sharpened blade give it the distinct impression of being cherished, and the potent scent of freshly chopped wood always clings to the axe's blade despite any attempt to clean it or remove the odor. A creature that holds or carries this _+2 striking [cold iron](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2916) fungus and plant [bane](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1041) [battle axe](/Weapons.aspx?ID=371)_ feels an obligation to tell the truth and receives a –4 status penalty to its attempts to Lie. 

**Activate** <actions string="" /> 1 minute (Interact);  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You polish and sharpen the axe, after which its scent grows even more powerful and the axe's blade transforms into your choice of standard-grade [adamantine](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2915) or standard-grade [mithral](/Equipment.aspx?ID=275) for 1 hour; then after this duration, the woodcutter's axe reverts to cold iron.

</column>

---

This unassuming tool wouldn’t look out of place on the belt of an industrious laborer. Grooves worn into the wooden handle over years of use and an irregularly sharpened blade give it the distinct impression of being cherished, and the potent scent of freshly chopped wood always clings to the axe’s blade despite any attempt to clean it or remove the odor. A creature that holds or carries this _[+2 striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2861) [cold iron](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2916) [battle axe](/Weapons.aspx?ID=371)_ feels an obligation to tell the truth and receives a –4 status penalty to its attempts to [Lie](/Actions.aspx?ID=2389). A lumber lord’s axe deals 1d6 additional slashing damage to creatures with the [fungus](/Traits.aspx?ID=614) or [plant](/Traits.aspx?ID=668) trait, as long as the creatures aren’t disguised as non-fungus or non-plant creatures. It’s up to GM discretion whether this additional damage applies against a creature disguised as a fungus or plant creature.

**Activate—Transformative Polish** <actions string="" /> 1 minute ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You polish and sharpen the axe, after which its scent grows even more powerful and the axe’s blade transforms into your choice of [standard-grade adamantine](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2915) or [standard-grade dawnsilver](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2917) for 1 hour; then after this duration, the woodcutter’s axe reverts to [cold iron](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2916).

>
[Lung Bloodstone of Arazni](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3785)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Claws of the Tyrant</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Unique" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=161" />
<trait label="Artifact" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=253" />
<trait label="Divine" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=48" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Claws of the Tyrant](/Sources.aspx?ID=266) pg. 109

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** 1
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

The _Lung Bloodstone of Arazni_ represents suffering. While you carry the _Lung Bloodstone_, you gain the ability to turn your pain into a weapon against your enemies.

**Activate—Strength through Pain** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per hour; **Trigger** You take damage;  **Effect** You allow the pain to resonate within you, making you stronger. You gain a +1 status bonus to your next [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) or [spell attack](/Rules.aspx?ID=2292) before the end of your next turn.

**Activate—Admonish** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=541), [emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=590), [incapacitation](/Traits.aspx?ID=631), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647)) **Frequency** once per day;  **Requirements** You worship [Arazni](/Deities.aspx?ID=326) or are favored by her; **Effect** You point your finger at a creature within 60 feet that has wronged you, and you verbally admonish them. The creature takes 1d4 [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647) damage for every level you have ([basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2297) Will save against your class DC). On a failed save, the creature is also [stunned](/Conditions.aspx?ID=93) 1 (stunned 3 on a critical failure).

**Destruction** To destroy the _Lung Bloodstone_, a worshipper of Arazni must willingly impale themself with the _Bloodstone’s_ horned figurehead, dealing themselves 3d6 piercing damage and 3d6 [persistent bleed damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=86). The _Lung Bloodstone_ then evaporates into a cloud of noxious vapors, as [_toxic cloud_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1722) (DC 28), that follows the creature that destroyed the _Bloodstone_ for its duration.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 5"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[Mad Mammoth's Juke](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1505)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Quest for the Frozen Flame</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Conjuration" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=33" />
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=36" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Talisman" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=155" />
<trait label="Teleportation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=156" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #175: Broken Tusk Moon](/Sources.aspx?ID=112) pg. 76

**Price** 30 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** affixed to armor

</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Free Action" /><row>envision</row></row>

 

**Trigger** You would be injured by an effect that would bury you, such as an avalanche or a tunnel collapse

**Requirement** You are an expert in [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1).
</row>

</column>

---

This small, fragile tusk came from a very young mammoth. It's filled with ice-cold glacial water and capped with a carved piece of ivory. When you crush the tusk, the water rushes around you in an instant as you twist away from impending disaster with a supernatural flourish. You teleport to an unoccupied space within 200 feet that you can see, bringing along all your equipment. You can't bring any other creature with you, even in an [extradimensional](/Traits.aspx?ID=67) space.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>
